sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: Which Texas-registered vehicles must pass a yearly official inspection, and what proof must you present at the station?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: Every motor vehicle registered in Texas passes a yearly check at an official inspection station, motorcycles, mopeds, scooters, and autocycles included, with insurance proof for that vehicle shown at inspection time.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: How does one windshield sticker prove both registration and inspection, and how long does a passing report count toward registration?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: A single valid windshield sticker now proves both registration and inspection together, the station prints a passing Vehicle Inspection Report into an electronic database the motor vehicle department confirms at registration, and that report stays valid ninety days from the inspection month for registration purposes.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: How does the annual inspection cycle differ from how long a passing report counts toward registration?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: Inspections repeat every year, yet each passing report only counts ninety days from its inspection month toward registration.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: From twenty miles per hour, within what distance must your foot brake stop the car, and what must the parking brake do?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.memory_hook: Twenty-five feet from twenty, parking holds
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: Safe cars need a foot brake that halts within twenty-five feet from twenty miles per hour plus a parking brake strong enough to stop and hold the car.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: What headlights, taillights, brake lamps, plate and parking lights, red reflectors, and electric turn signals are required to pass inspection?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.memory_hook: Full working lights, reflectors, turn signals
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: Lighting rules demand two headlights with a high-beam indicator, two taillights or one on pre-nineteen-sixty cars, two working brake lights or one on pre-nineteen-sixty cars with all three lit where a center high lamp is fitted, a white rear plate light, white-or-amber front and red rear parking lights, two red side reflectors set fifteen to sixty inches high and seen six hundred feet out or three hundred fifty on pre-nineteen-sixty cars, and electric turn signals on most trailers and vehicles except motorcycles and narrow pre-nineteen-sixty cars under eighty inches wide.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: How do minimum taillight and brake-light counts differ between modern cars and pre-nineteen-sixty cars?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.memory_hook: Modern cars two, older cars one
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: Modern cars carry two taillights and two brake lights, while pre-nineteen-sixty cars need only one of each.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: Between what heights must red reflectors sit, and how far out must they be visible on modern versus pre-nineteen-sixty cars?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.memory_hook: Fifteen to sixty, six hundred feet
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: Reflectors sit fifteen to sixty inches high and show six hundred feet out, except pre-nineteen-sixty cars whose reflectors show three hundred fifty feet.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: Beyond brakes and lights, what standards cover horns, emissions, safety glass, plates, wipers, mirrors, slow emblems, belts, tread, and fuel caps?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.memory_hook: Horn, mirror, tread, emissions, fuel cap
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: Further required gear includes a horn heard two hundred feet away, emission controls on nineteen-sixty-eight and later models, safety glass for new and replacement panes, front and rear plates except single-plate dealer and commercial issues, wipers, a mirror reaching two hundred feet behind, slow-moving emblems on rigs capped at twenty-five miles per hour, front belts where anchorages came factory-fitted, tires holding two thirty-seconds of an inch, and a sound fuel cap on gasoline vehicles aged two to twenty-four years outside antique, circus, slow, motorcycle, and alternate-fuel exceptions.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: What exact distance standard do both a vehicle's horn and its rearview mirror share?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.memory_hook: Two hundred feet front and back
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: Both the horn and the rearview mirror share a two-hundred-foot standard, the horn heard that far and the mirror seeing that far behind.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: Which front lights, warning noisemakers, exhaust mods, side overhangs, and radar devices are illegal on ordinary vehicles?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.memory_hook: No front red, sirens, cutouts, jammers
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: Banned gear covers front red lights, bells, sirens, exhaust whistles, muffler cutouts, loads jutting over three inches left or six inches right, front flashing red lights, and radar-jamming devices, with emergency vehicles and school or church buses keeping their narrow allowances.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: How far may cargo jut past the fenders on the left side versus the right side, and who alone may display front red lights?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.memory_hook: Three left, six right, emergency red
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: Loads may poke three inches past the left side but six inches past the right, and front red lights stay banned for everyone except emergency vehicles.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: How low may a car body ride, and what rules govern optional spotlights, cowl, courtesy, backup, hazard, extra driving lights, and window tint?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: No car may ride with its body below the lowest wheel rims, while optional spotlights dim for oncoming traffic or cast fifty feet in headlight failure, twin cowl lights and single side courtesy lights glow amber or white, twin backup lights never burn moving forward, hazard flashers blink amber-white ahead and amber-red behind in unison, up to three extra driving lamps sit twelve to forty-two inches high, and any tinting obeys state rules.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: When must an optional spotlight be switched off, and how far ahead may it shine if your main headlights go out?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.memory_hook: Off for oncoming, fifty-foot backup beam
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: Spotlights switch off for oncoming drivers, yet may light fifty feet of road when the headlights themselves fail.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: Where do vehicles register and wear stickers, what are the thirty-day and sixty-day windows, and how do metal versus cardboard dealer tags differ?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.memory_hook: Home county, thirty purchase, no cardboard
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: Vehicles register in the owner's home county with the sticker on the windshield or the rear plate of a bike or moped, fresh purchases register within thirty days, nonresident farm trucks may draw thirty-day harvest permits, buyer tags last sixty days, dealer and manufacturer plates still need inspection, and cardboard dealer tags cover demos, hauls, and service without inspection yet never driving exams.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: How does the deadline to register a newly bought vehicle compare with how long a buyer temporary tag stays valid?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.memory_hook: Register within thirty, buyer tag sixty
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: Fresh purchases must register within thirty days, while buyer temporary tags remain good sixty days.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: Which household trips are allowed on farm-registered vehicles, what work use is forbidden, and where do registration questions go?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.memory_hook: Family errands allowed, paid jobs banned
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: Farm-registered vehicles may also ferry family to church, school, doctors, and household needs but never serve gainful employment, and registration questions go to the county tax assessor-collector or the motor vehicle department.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: What must new Texans do with owned vehicles before getting a license, what thirty-day grace applies, and what three items does registration require?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.memory_hook: Inspect, insure, register before Texas license
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: New Texans register every owned vehicle before seeking a license, fresh residents and new jobholders get thirty days of operation first, registration demands a Texas inspection report plus VIN verification and insurance proof with no insurance meaning no registration, and the county receipt doubles as registration proof at licensing.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: How does the thirty-day grace window for new arrivals or jobholders pair with registering vehicles before licensing?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.memory_hook: Thirty days first, register before licensing
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: New residents register everything before licensing, while newcomers who just arrived or just started work get thirty days of driving first.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: Which seven farm, sweeping, golf-cart, e-bike, or mobility vehicles need no registration, inspection, or plates for temporary highway travel?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.memory_hook: Tractors, light farm trailers, e-bikes exempt
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: Temporary highway use needs no registration, inspection, or plates for farm tractors, light farm and fertilizer or cottonseed trailers at four thousand pounds or less, farm implements, power sweepers, certain golf carts, electric bicycles, and personal mobility devices.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: Which machinery and mid-weight farm trailers travel under Texas's annual five-dollar distinguishing plate?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.memory_hook: Machinery and mid-heavy trailers, five-dollar plate
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: Well-drilling and construction machinery plus heavier farm, cotton, and fertilizer trailers between four thousand and thirty-four thousand pounds run on an annual five-dollar distinguishing plate with the law's extra conditions.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: Which exact weight threshold divides fully exempt farm trailers from those needing the annual five-dollar distinguishing plate?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.memory_hook: Four thousand exempt, thirty-four thousand plated
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: Light farm trailers at four thousand pounds or less run fully exempt, while heavier farm trailers to thirty-four thousand pounds need the annual five-dollar plate.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: Under the Texas Safety Responsibility Act, what harms are vehicle owners and drivers financially answerable for causing, and what minimum coverage is required?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: The Texas Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act makes every owner and operator of a motor vehicle financially answerable for death, injury, or property damage they cause, with at least minimum liability insurance required.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: What are the three minimum dollar amounts for Texas auto liability coverage across one victim, two or more victims, and property damage?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: Minimum liability coverage runs thirty thousand dollars for injury or death of one person, sixty thousand dollars for two or more people, and twenty-five thousand dollars for property damage.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: How do Texas's three required liability caps split between one injured person, two or more people, and damaged property?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.memory_hook: One thirty, group sixty, property twenty-five
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: Minimums split three ways, thirty thousand dollars for one person, sixty thousand dollars for two or more, and twenty-five thousand dollars for property.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: Unless exempt or self-insured, during which three routine errands must you show insurance proof, and which two people can request it on the road?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: Every driver keeps liability insurance or qualifies as self-insured unless exempt, shows proof when licensing, registering, or inspecting, and hands proof to any officer on request or any person involved in a crash.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: How does Texas separate routine paperwork visits that require insurance proof from on-demand moments when you must hand it over?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: Proof is shown routinely at licensing, registration, and inspection, yet on demand to officers and crash counterparts.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: Which three policy-based documents count as accepted Texas liability proof, and what details must appear on the standard proof form?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: Accepted proof starts with a minimum-limits policy, a standard insurance-department proof form naming insurer, policy number and period, each insured party, limits or a compliance statement, and each covered vehicle's make and model, plus a compliance-showing insurance binder.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: Beyond an insurance policy, which four deposit, bond, or fleet certificates prove Texas financial responsibility, including their dollar and vehicle thresholds?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: Further proof includes a comptroller certificate over a fifty-five-thousand-dollar money or securities deposit, a DPS surety bond on file, a county-judge certificate over a fifty-five-thousand-dollar cash or cashier's check deposit, or a DPS self-insurance certificate for owners of more than twenty-five vehicles.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: What exact dollar deposit backs both comptroller and county-judge certificates, and how many vehicles must an owner hold to self-insure?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: Both the comptroller certificate and the county-judge certificate rest on fifty-five thousand dollars deposited, while self-insurance rests on owning more than twenty-five vehicles.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: Does a phone image count as Texas insurance proof, what happens if proof is missing, and when can a court dismiss that ticket?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.memory_hook: Phone image counts, active policy dismisses
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: A wireless-device image carrying the standard-form facts also proves coverage, missing proof draws a citation, and courts may dismiss when a policy covered the citation moment.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: What fine range hits a first Texas conviction without proof of insurance, and what fines, license penalty, and impound rule hit repeat convictions?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: Conviction without sufficient proof fines one hundred seventy-five to three hundred fifty dollars first, then suspends the license, fines three hundred fifty to one thousand dollars, and court-impounds an owner-driven vehicle one hundred eighty days with proof due before release.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: How does the court outcome for missing proof when a valid policy covered you compare with a conviction when you had no coverage?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: A citation for missing proof dies when coverage existed, but conviction without coverage brings fines and worse.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: How do the penalties for a first Texas no-insurance conviction differ from a second or later conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: First convictions end in fines alone, while second and later ones add suspension, bigger fines, and a one-hundred-eighty-day impoundment.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: Which three conviction, unpaid-judgment, or payment-plan failures trigger suspension of your Texas tags, license, or driving privilege?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: Registration, license, or privilege suspends after a suspendable traffic conviction lacking insurance proof to DPS, an unpaid crash judgment past sixty days, or a defaulted crash-installment agreement.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: Which uninsured crash harms trigger suspension when a judgment looks likely, and how long must proof stay on file after your latest conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: Suspension also follows an uninsured crash killing, injuring, or inflicting one thousand dollars of property damage where judgment looks likely, and proof must be maintained two years from the latest conviction date.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: How does the deadline for paying off a crash judgment compare with how long you must keep insurance proof after your latest conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.memory_hook: Sixty days judgment, two years proof
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: Crash judgments must be satisfied within sixty days, while proof itself must be kept two years from the latest conviction.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: Which three outcomes of an uninsured crash, paired with a likely court judgment, trigger a Texas suspension review?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: An uninsured crash triggers suspension review through death, injury, or one thousand dollars of property damage with likely judgment.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: Which state web pages and which Austin office provide deeper guidance on Texas financial-responsibility compliance?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: Deeper compliance guidance lives on the DPS financial-responsibility pages and with the Enforcement and Compliance Service in Austin.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: Why must you stay alert after pulling into a spot, and what four steps belong in every park-and-exit routine?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: Parked cars can still cause crashes, so drivers kill the motor, set the brake, pocket the key, and check behind for traffic before swinging doors open.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: Which roadway spots forbid parking, stopping, or even briefly standing at the wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: Nothing may park, stop, or stand idling roadside of a parked car, on sidewalks or crosswalks, inside intersections, between safety zones and curbs or within thirty feet opposite their ends, beside excavations that block traffic, on bridges, elevated spans, tunnels, rails, or where signs ban stopping.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: Even with someone sitting inside, what are the no-park and no-stand zones and exact setbacks at driveways, hydrants, crosswalks, signals, and fire stations?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: Occupied or not, vehicles never park or stand ahead of driveways, within fifteen feet of hydrants, within twenty feet of intersection crosswalks, within thirty feet before roadside signals and signs, within twenty feet of fire-station doors or seventy-five feet across from them, or where signs ban parking or standing.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: How far from railroad tracks is parking banned, what rules govern rural highway parking, and when may a bicycle park on a sidewalk?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: Parking alone is further banned within fifty feet of rails and where signs ban it, rural highways demand off-road parking or else passing room plus two-hundred-foot visibility both ways with night lights or dim headlamps, and bicycles may rest on sidewalks that stay passable.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: How do Texas curb rules step down across the strictest, middle, and lightest restriction tiers?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: The strictest bans block parking, stopping, and standing alike, the middle bans block parking and standing, and the lightest bans block parking only.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: What are the exact footage setbacks for hydrants, crosswalks, station doors, signals, safety zones, railroad tracks, and opposite fire stations?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: Setbacks run fifteen feet at hydrants, twenty feet at crosswalks and station doors, thirty feet at signals and safety zones, fifty feet at rails, and seventy-five feet across from stations.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: What is your first choice when parking on a rural highway, and what three requirements apply if you cannot clear the pavement?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: Rural parking leaves the pavement entirely, or else leaves passing room with two-hundred-foot sight lines and night lamps.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: How is disabled-parking abuse classified, how do fines escalate from first to fifth offense, and do traffic-sign stops count as parking?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: Disabled-space abuse is a misdemeanor fining five hundred to seven hundred fifty dollars first and climbing to one thousand two hundred fifty dollars plus community service by the fifth offense, while obedience stops for signs and signals never count as parking or standing.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: What dollar range opens disabled-parking fines, what penalty hits by offense five, and why is obeying a stop sign different?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: Disabled abuse fines start five hundred to seven hundred fifty dollars and reach one thousand two hundred fifty dollars plus service, while sign-obedience stops are never parking at all.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: Who must be transported to use a disabled plate or placard, what placard abuses are illegal, and which access areas must stay clear?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: Disabled spaces need plates or removable windshield cards used only while carrying the holder, cards stay unlent, ramps stay unblocked, counterfeits and alterations stay criminal, some cities also ban stopping or standing there, and striped lift zones stay empty.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: Can you borrow or alter someone else's disabled placard for a quick errand, and how are ramps and striped zones treated?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: Cards ride only with their holders, never lent or forged, with ramps and striped lift zones equally protected.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: What five steps are legally required before leaving a vehicle unattended, and how do remote-start systems fit into that rule?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: Unattended idling breaks the law without engine-off, locked ignition, removed key, set brake, and grade-parked wheels to the curb, though remote starters skip the key rules until a key rides along to drive.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: What five steps secure an unattended car, and what makes a remote-started vehicle legal before someone drives off?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: Unattended cars need engine off, ignition locked, key out, brake set, and grade wheels curbed, except remote-started cars whose keys join before driving.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: How do you line up and begin backing into a parallel spot, and what is the maximum curb distance on a two-way street?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: Parallel parking starts with a roomy space, an early signal, and a stop even with the lead car two feet out, then hard-right wheels backing curbward clear of oncoming cars, while two-way streets park right wheels within eighteen inches of the curb.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: Which two measurements govern your starting gap beside the front car and your final curb limit on two-way streets?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: Parallel setups stage two feet out beside lead cars, while two-way streets cap curb distance at eighteen inches.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: When do you cut the wheel hard left during a parallel park, how close to the curb do you aim, and how do you finish?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: Parallel finishes swing hard left once seats meet bumpers, back to six inches from the curb and never beyond eighteen, then straighten centered in the space.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: What rules govern wheel angle on hills, pulling out from parked spots near kids, residential awareness, and coasting downhill?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.memory_hook: Angle wheels, scan kids, stay geared
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: Hill parking aims wheels curbward with or without curbs as diagrammed, departures check mirrors and backs for children between cars with exit signals, residential drivers watch for children, and downhill neutral coasting stays illegal.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: What are the ideal and maximum parallel curb distances, the hill-wheel rule, and the downhill transmission rule?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: Parallel finishes land six inches from the curb inside an eighteen-inch ceiling, hills angle wheels to curbs, and neutral coasting stays banned.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: How should your speed blend with traffic, how many seconds do experienced and beginner drivers keep at different speeds, and what defines tailgating?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Drivers match the traffic stream while honoring every limit, keeping two seconds behind leaders at thirty miles per hour or less, four seconds above thirty, more in poor conditions, four seconds always for beginners, and any fixed-object gap under two seconds marks tailgating.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: Where does the following-distance rule jump from two seconds to four, what gap do beginners hold, and how do you measure it?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: Gaps run two seconds at thirty miles per hour or less and four seconds above, with beginners holding four always and fixed-object checks catching tailgaters.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: How long does average driver reaction take, and how far does total dry-pavement stopping distance jump from twenty to seventy miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Average drivers need one and a half seconds to think, react, and brake, and total stopping stretches climb from sixty-three feet at twenty miles per hour to three hundred eighty-seven feet at seventy with good brakes and tires on dry level pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: What reaction time precedes braking, and which two benchmark stopping distances show the leap from twenty to seventy miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: Reaction alone eats one and a half seconds, while full stops stretch from sixty-three feet at twenty miles per hour to three hundred eighty-seven at seventy.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: Which three factors govern safe speed and space, when must you stay off the road entirely, and how do weather or darkness change your pace?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: Speed and gaps flex with driver fitness, vehicle state, and road state, tired or ill drivers stay parked, wet, crowded, and blind conditions earn slower wider driving with full control, and nobody outdrives visible road in dark or weather.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: What two adjustments apply on wet, crowded, or restricted-view roads, and what is the golden rule for night speed?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: Wet, crowded, and blind roads each earn slower wider driving, and darkness forbids outdriving headlight vision.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: How wide is your field of vision when stationary, and what fraction remains at twenty, forty, and sixty miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Vision spans one hundred eighty degrees or more standing still, then shrinks to about two-thirds at twenty miles per hour, two-fifths at forty, and one-fifth at sixty.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: At twenty, forty, and sixty miles per hour, what fraction of your standing-still field of vision remains?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Sight fields fall from full width standing still to two-thirds at twenty, two-fifths at forty, and one-fifth at sixty miles per hour.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: When do posted minimums and maximums apply, when must you drop below them, and what restriction binds city or county speed changes?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Posted minimums and maximums bind under normal flow, heavy traffic, weather, and gloom demand slower wider driving, and cities and counties may reset limits but must hold day and night equal.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: What are the default Texas statutory speed limits in urban districts, alleys, and declared beaches or adjacent county roads?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: Maximums run thirty miles per hour in urban districts, fifteen in alleys, and fifteen on beaches and beach-adjacent county roads where declared.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: Outside urban districts, what default limits govern cars and school buses on numbered versus unnumbered roads, and how high can posted freeways go?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.memory_hook: Seventy numbered, sixty unnumbered, signs rule
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: Outside urban districts numbered highways allow seventy miles per hour generally or sixty for inspected school buses, unnumbered roads allow sixty generally or fifty for uninspected or off-system school buses, studies may raise or lower limits, many limited-access highways post seventy-five to eighty-five, and posted signs always rule.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: How do Texas default speed tiers step up from alleys, beaches, and urban streets to rural roads, buses, and freeways?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: Surface caps read thirty urban and fifteen alley or beach, highway caps read seventy or sixty numbered and sixty or fifty unnumbered with school-bus steps down, and freeways often post seventy-five to eighty-five.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: Which six types of flashing roadside vehicles trigger Texas's move-over law, and what two compliance options do you have?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Past lit stopped medical, law, fire, tow, utility, and road-work vehicles drivers drop twenty below the limit or abandon the nearest lane on multi-lane roads.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: How should you handle passing mail carriers, delivery vans, and trash trucks that make frequent stops?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: Mail, delivery, and trash trucks stopping often earn cautious passing with lane changes where possible.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: How does your legal duty passing flashing rescue, tow, or work rigs differ from passing stopped mail or trash vehicles?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: Lit work and rescue stops demand twenty below the limit or a lane away, while mail and trash stops want caution and room.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: Which five forms of racing or speed competition are illegal on Texas roads, and what criminal charges can a conviction carry?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: Street racing bans races, speed contests, drag and acceleration contests, driver endurance tests, and drag-linked speed exhibitions or records, punishing convictions from Class B misdemeanor to second-degree felony for the deadly crashes and road damage they bring.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: How broad is Texas's ban on racing events, and what is the full range of conviction levels?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: Five racing forms stay banned from plain races through exhibitions and records, with penalties spanning Class B misdemeanor to second-degree felony.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: Which legal or illegal substances can impair driving, which four personal factors change the impact, and what three traits does safe driving require?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.memory_hook: Sharp eyes, steady hands, clear head
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Every drug can dull driving, from store-bought and prescribed medicines through illegal drugs and alcohol, striking the mental and physical skills behind emergency reactions, varying by body weight, mood, dose, and timing, while safe driving always wants observant eyes, steady hands, and clear heads.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: Which two driving abilities do alcohol and drugs attack first, what happens when substances mix, and who should check every medicine combination?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Drink and drugs first steal judgment and sight, slowing sound reactions and wrecking speed estimates until reason vanishes, mixed drugs stack dangers with alcohol masking companions, so doctors or pharmacists preview every combination especially tranquilizers and sedatives.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: What four variables make impairment hit people differently, and which two abilities still drop first every time?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.memory_hook: Four factors vary, judgment drops first
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: Impairment varies by weight, mood, dose, and timing, yet always attacks judgment and sight first.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: When an arrested minor operates a vehicle or watercraft with any detectable alcohol, what specimens and substances does implied consent cover, and what happens even without a license on refusal?

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: What are the exact side-by-side suspension lengths for minor test refusals versus minor detectable-alcohol failures?

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: How do fines, community-service hours, classes, jail time, and interlock options escalate across first, second, and third minor DUI offenses?

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: What penalties hit minors convicted of full DWI across first, second, and third offenses — plus with an open container, a child under fifteen, assault, or manslaughter?

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: For which two minor convictions can a judge-ordered ignition interlock trim a full year of license suspension down to ninety days?

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: Under adult implied consent, how many suspension days follow a first or repeat test refusal versus failing at point zero eight or higher?

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: What fines, confinement ranges, and license suspensions apply to adult DWI from first through third offenses, child-passenger cases, assault, and manslaughter?

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: How do adult refusal days compare with adult failure days on first and repeat stops, and where do repeat or severe DWI charges lead?

sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: Adult refusals cost one hundred eighty then up to seven hundred thirty days, failures cost ninety then up to three hundred sixty-five, and offense ladders climb through felonies.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: What three mistakes cause most Texas crashes, what details must drivers swap and log at the scene, and what if the other driver lacks insurance info?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.memory_hook: Copy insurer and policy number exact
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Most Texas crashes trace to speeding, botched yielding or stopping, and alcohol impairment, and crash drivers trade names, addresses, phones, vehicle numbers, plate numbers, license facts, and insurance facts when asked and available, copying insurer names and policy numbers verbatim while insurer gaps go to the insurance department hotline, plus crash locations and witness contacts.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: Which three driving errors top Texas crash stats, and how carefully must you write down insurance details?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.memory_hook: Speed, yield, alcohol, copy policy exact
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Top causes run speeding, bad yielding, and drink, while exchanges run names through insurance with verbatim policy copies.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: Which four crash situations require notifying law enforcement immediately right from the scene?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: Law enforcement hears immediately about injuries or deaths, immovable vehicles, fleeing drivers, and suspected intoxication.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: When police do not investigate a minor crash without injury, death, or one thousand dollars in damage, what report is needed and by what deadline?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Uninvestigated crashes without injury, death, or one thousand dollars of property damage need a written transportation-department report on its form within ten days of the crash.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: How does Texas split immediate police-call crashes from ten-day written-report crashes?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.memory_hook: Four call police, ten days minor
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: Four triggers summon police at once, while minor uninvestigated crashes file written reports within ten days under one thousand dollars.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: What stopping, identification, and medical-aid duties apply immediately when a crash injures or kills someone?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.memory_hook: Stop, stay, share info, render aid
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: Injury-or-death crashes demand immediate stops at or near scenes without needless obstruction plus immediate returns and stays, handing name, address, registration, and insurer to injured parties and vehicle attendants, flashing licenses when asked and available, and rendering reasonable aid including doctor-or-hospital transport when needed or requested.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: After a crash that damages only attended vehicles, when and where must you move a drivable car before exchanging information?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.memory_hook: Drivable main-lane crash: pull clear first

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: What is the key action difference between stopping for an injury crash and stopping for a drivable vehicle-only crash?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.memory_hook: Hurt needs aid, drivable moves clear

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: What prison terms and maximum fines punish fleeing a crash involving death, serious bodily injury, or other injury?

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: How do criminal charge levels step down across death, serious bodily injury, and other injury in a hit-and-run?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.memory_hook: Second-degree death, third-degree serious, prison injury
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: Fleeing death draws second-degree felony years, serious injury draws third-degree felony years, and plain injury draws prison or jail plus fines.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: What dollar threshold splits vehicle-damage hit-and-run penalties, and what fines or jail apply on each side of it?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.memory_hook: Two hundred dollars triggers Class B

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: At what exact damage amount does fleeing a property-only crash jump from a Class C fine to Class B jail time?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.memory_hook: Under two hundred C, above B
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: Property-only fleeing splits at two hundred dollars, Class C below and Class B with jail above.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: If you bump a parked unattended car, what must you do if you cannot find the owner, what goes in the note, and what penalties apply for leaving?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.memory_hook: Find owner or leave visible note

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: What duties, reporting deadline, and fleeing penalties apply if your vehicle strikes highway landscaping, a signpost, or another roadside fixture?

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: How do your legal options differ after hitting an unattended parked car versus hitting a roadside fixture or landscaping?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.memory_hook: Cars allow notes, fixtures need notice
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: Unattended cars get found owners or visible notes, while fixtures get found owners, notice, and possible ten-day reports.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: Why must hit-and-run victims file a police report for insurance, and what five rules guide bystanders helping an injured crash victim?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.memory_hook: Report hit-and-runs, never move injured victims
