sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: What protects a hit-and-run victim's uninsured-motorist claim, and which five essentials protect an injured person at a crash scene?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.memory_hook: Report for coverage, pad, keep still
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Hit-and-runs need police reports for coverage, and injured victims need clear locations, skilled help, stillness, pressure pads, and shelter.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: How does Texas traffic law classify a bicycle, and what rights and duties apply to its rider?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: Texas treats a bicycle as a vehicle, so a rider holds the same rights and owes the same duties as any vehicle driver except where a rule cannot by its nature fit a bicycle.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: If you break a traffic law on a bicycle, how does the penalty compare to a car, and where does a conviction land?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: Breaking a traffic law on a bicycle draws the same penalty as breaking it in a motor vehicle, and every traffic conviction goes on the rider's driver record no matter which one they were operating.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: How must a cyclist treat traffic laws, stop signs, and red lights?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: Riders obey every traffic law, sign, and signal, halting at each stop sign and red light.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: In which direction must a bicyclist ride compared to surrounding traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: Riders always travel with the flow of traffic and never ride against it.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: What two foundational rules govern a bicyclist's travel direction and signal obedience?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: Bicycles travel with traffic and obey every signal, never against the flow.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: Where may a cyclist ride on a one-way street that has two or more marked lanes?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: On a one-way road with at least two marked lanes, a rider keeps as close as possible to the left curb or edge.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: Where does a slower cyclist normally ride, and which four situations allow moving away from the right curb?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: A rider moving slower than surrounding traffic stays as close as possible to the right curb or edge, except when passing another vehicle, preparing a left turn, avoiding hazards such as parked cars or debris, or riding an outside lane narrower than fourteen feet or too tight for a bicycle and car to travel side by side.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: How does a cyclist's curb edge position on a multi-lane one-way street compare to slower riding elsewhere?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: One-way multilane roads push riders toward the left edge while slower-than-traffic riding keeps them at the right edge.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: Under what two conditions may two cyclists ride abreast on a laned roadway?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: Two riders side by side on a laned road share one lane and must not block the movement of traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: Does Texas law allow a bicyclist to ride on the paved shoulder of a roadway?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: Riders are allowed to use the shoulder of the road.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: What four safety benefits do shared lane pavement markings provide for cyclists and drivers?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: Shared lane markings help riders position themselves away from opening car doors and in lanes too narrow to share, show road users where riders are likely to be, promote safe passing, and discourage wrong-way riding.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: How do road shoulders, riding in pairs, and shared lane arrows each work for cyclists?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: Shoulders welcome riders, side-by-side pairs share a single lane without blocking cars, and shared markings guide placement.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: Which specific arm positions do cyclists use to signal a right turn, a left turn, and a stop?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: Riders signal with their arms: a right turn means the left arm up or the right arm held flat, a left turn means the left arm held flat, and a stop means the left arm pointed down.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: How do the two right-turn arm options differ from the left-turn and stop arm signals?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: Right turns flash left-arm-up or right-arm-flat, left turns use left-arm-flat, and stops drop the left arm.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: How must a cyclist sit while riding, and how many riders may a bicycle carry?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: A rider sits only on or astride a permanent regular seat and never carries more people than the bicycle was designed or equipped to hold.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: May a bicyclist grab or attach onto a moving vehicle or streetcar on the roadway?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: A rider never hitches the bicycle or their body to a moving streetcar or vehicle on the road.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: What limit applies to carrying packages, bundles, or objects while riding a bicycle?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: A rider never carries a package, bundle, or object that stops them from keeping at least one hand on the handlebars.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: Which three rider conduct rules govern bicycle seating, moving vehicles, and carrying items?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: Seats carry only designed riders, hitching to moving vehicles stays banned, and one hand always grips the bars.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: What exact stopping standard must every bicycle's brake meet in Texas?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: Each bicycle needs a brake strong enough to skid its wheels on dry, level, clean pavement.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: What equipment may a bicyclist with hearing loss display on their bike?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: Riders with hearing loss may show a safety flag on the bicycle.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: What front and rear night equipment must a bicycle carry, and from what distances must each required or optional item show?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: At night a bicycle carries a front white lamp seen from at least five hundred feet ahead plus a red DPS-approved rear reflector seen from fifty to three hundred feet, with an optional red rear light seen from five hundred feet allowed alongside the reflector.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: When riding after dark, which two items are mandatory on a bike and which rear item is optional?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: Night demands a white front lamp and a red rear reflector, with an optional red rear lamp allowed too.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: At what level of government can bicycle helmet rules be made mandatory?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: Local laws may require a rider to wear a helmet.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: How should cyclists handle shared walkways, parked car rows, and stopping or fixing a bike?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: Riders slow down and stay careful on walkways shared with pedestrians, never weave between parked cars, and pull fully off the street to stop, park, or fix the bicycle.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: How should a cyclist choose routes, and what gear or clothing helps drivers spot them?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: Riders pick routes that fit their skill and experience, may fit a mirror, and wear light or reflective clothing so drivers can spot them.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: Which three specific hazards must a bicyclist watch out for when riding in the rain?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: In rain, riders watch for slick manholes and painted stripes, hidden water-filled potholes, and drivers whose visibility drops sharply.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: How do local helmet ordinances, route choices, visibility gear, and rainy conditions tie together for cyclists?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: Helmets follow local law, routes fit rider skill, mirrors and bright clothing aid visibility, and rain hides hazards.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: Whose directions override traffic signals and ordinary laws, where do you stop on steady red, and which two turns on red are lawful after yielding?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Drivers obey every signal unless an officer directs otherwise, and officer orders stand even against ordinary law, with steady red demanding a stop ahead of the crosswalk or intersection before any lawful right turn or any left turn joining one one-way street from another, always yielding to pedestrians and legal intersection users.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: What action is required on flashing red, steady or flashing yellow, flashing yellow left arrows, steady green, and green arrows beside red?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: Flashing red means stop fully then go when safe while cross traffic may roll on, steady yellow orders a safe stop or a cautious clearing, flashing yellow orders slower caution, flashing yellow left arrows permit left turns against yielding to oncoming cars, steady green permits straight or turning travel with intersection watchfulness, green arrows beside red permit careful arrow-direction travel after yielding, and plain green lefts yield to all oncoming traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: After making a complete stop, how do your travel options at a steady red light differ from a flashing red light?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: Steady red stops before turns that stay conditional, while flashing red stops fully before a safe unconditioned go.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: How do your duties differ across a steady yellow light, a flashing yellow light, and a flashing yellow left arrow?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.memory_hook: Steady stops, flashing slows, arrow yields
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: Steady yellow demands a safe stop or cautious clearing, flashing yellow only slower caution, and flashing yellow left arrows add oncoming-yield duty.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: How does driving on a steady green light compare with following a green arrow displayed beside a red light?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: Steady green goes with intersection vigilance and yielding lefts, while green arrows beside red go carefully in the arrow's path after yielding.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: What four core jobs do roadway traffic signs perform for drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: Traffic signs warn of hidden hazards ahead, guide travelers along routes, publish local rules and habits, and regulate speed and movement.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: What meaning belongs to red, green, blue, yellow, black-and-white, orange, reflective orange, and brown road signs?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.memory_hook: Red stops, orange work, brown parks
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: Sign colors read red for stop, yield, or posted orders, green for allowed moves and direction, blue for motorist services, yellow for warning, black and white for regulation, orange for construction and maintenance, reflective orange for varied signs, and brown for recreation and scenery.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: What meaning belongs to each of the eight standard road-sign shapes, and what risk follows ignoring warning signs?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.memory_hook: Octagon stop, pennant no-pass, circle rail
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: Sign shapes read octagon for stop only, horizontal rectangle for guides, triangle for yield only, pennant for no-passing advance notice, diamond for hazard warnings, vertical rectangle for regulations, pentagon for school zones and crossings, and circle for railroad advance notice, with warning signs demanding attention, obedience, and posted-speed slowing under violation risk.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: How do red, yellow, orange, and brown pair up with octagon, triangle, diamond, and pennant sign shapes?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: Red orders, yellow warns, orange flags work zones, and brown guides recreation, matched by octagon stops, triangle yields, diamond warnings, and pennant no-pass notices.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: How must you respond to warnings for low clearance, medians, added lanes, right-then-left reverse curves, joining roads, rough pavement, and signals ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.memory_hook: Added lane flows, reverse curve slows
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: Warning signs call for different responses. Check the posted height before entering an underpass; a median sign announces divided traffic; an added-lane sign means watch the new lane without merging. At a right-then-left curve, reduce speed, stay right and avoid passing. Watch for vehicles from a joining road, slow for rough pavement and heed warnings of a signal or crossing traffic ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: What actions follow warnings for sharp or gradual curves, winding roads, divided-highway endings, wet pavement, two-way traffic, crossroads, and lane drops?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: Further warnings flag sharp arrowed turns, winding roads, divided-highway endings with returning two-way traffic, wet roads forbidding sudden moves, right-lane discipline against left-side oncoming cars, gradual arrowed curves, crossroads needing all-direction looks, and shrinking lane counts.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: How should you adjust speed, lane position, and passing for reverse curves, sharp turns, and gradual curves versus a winding road?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.memory_hook: Slow down, keep right, never pass
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: For reverse curves, sharp turns and gradual curves, reduce speed, stay right and avoid passing. For a winding road, travel slowly and cautiously without passing.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: What hazards and driver responses pair with warnings for T and Y junctions, merges, pedestrian or school areas, loose gravel, pier obstructions, and alignment shifts?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: More warnings mark T and Y junctions, merging lanes, heavy pedestrian zones, schools needing sudden-stop readiness, loose gravel forbidding sharp braking or turns, edge and pier obstruction markers, and short-alignment change markers.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: How should you handle warnings for T must-turns, dips, soft shoulders, narrow or icy bridges, highway junctions, double sharp turns, and night delineators?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Still more warnings order T must-turns with yielding, dip slowdowns, soft-shoulder caution, narrow-bridge care, highway-junction looks and stop readiness, double sharp turns, winter ice-bridge gentleness, and night-alignment delineators.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: Which four warning types belong to road junctions, and which four warn about changing road surfaces?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: Junction warnings cover T, Y, merges, and must-turns, while surface warnings cover gravel, dips, soft shoulders, and ice.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: What do warnings for traffic islands, bridge-rail ends, entering trucks, narrow or dirt transitions, edge drop-offs, wet-weather grooves, and wheelchair crossings tell you?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: Continuing warnings allow either-side island passing, mark narrow-bridge rail ends, announce entering trucks, narrow pavements, pavement-to-earth transitions, edge drop-offs needing firm slow steering, grooved wet-weather grooves cautioning motorcyclists, and disabled or wheelchair crossings.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: How do you respond to warnings for steep downgrades, metered ramps, sudden humps, sharp curves, ending right lanes, stop signs ahead, and animal crossings?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Final warnings announce downgrades possibly needing low gear, metered ramps with flashing yellows and red-green meters, sudden humps, sharp curves, ending right lanes merging left, stop signs ahead, and animals.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: What legal force do regulatory signs carry, and what rules do they set on arrow turns, weekday carpool hours, passing, double lefts, disabled spaces, and banned turns?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: Regulatory signs bind like traffic laws, covering arrow-only turns, bus and carpool lanes weekday mornings six to nine, sight-limited yellow-line no-passing, double left-turn lanes with a mandatory left lane, disabled parking reserved to placarded vehicles, banned lefts, banned U-turns, and wrong-way one-way entry.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: Why does slowing never satisfy a stop sign for any vehicle in line, and what other speed, passing, truck, and island rules appear on regulatory signs?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: More regulations order full stops with yielding and careful starts ahead of crosswalks and signs for every vehicle since slowing never suffices, plus advisory curve speeds, passing bans, slower-right discipline, safe ramp-exit speeds, posted day and night maximums, truck bans, and rightward island guidance.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: How does the legal demand of a stop sign compare with a posted curve advisory speed?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: Stop signs force full stops with yielding starts for every vehicle, while advisory speeds merely cap safe curve travel.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: What regulatory rules cover wrong-way entry, merging, flashing school zones, red-light cameras, double white lines, protected lefts, shoulders, detours, and single-file merges?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: Further regulations bar opposite-direction one-way entry, command merge-and-yield manners, enforce flashing-yellow school speeds with child watchfulness, warn of red-light cameras, forbid double-white-line crossings, protect green-arrow lefts while urging caution, reserve shoulders for breakdown and emergency stops, close roads to detours, and merge all traffic single-file.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: What rules govern highway crossovers, school-zone phone bans, all-way stop ties, passing-only left lanes, shared center turn lanes, and dedicated turn lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: Still more regulations mark divided-highway crossovers, ban wireless devices in school zones, run all-way stops by arrival order with right-side ties, push slower traffic off the passing-only far-left lane, confine center lanes to slowing or stopping left turns, green-light left turns, force right-lane right turns, and post advisory turn speeds.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: How do all-way stop tie-breakers, protected green arrows, center left-turn lanes, and passing-only far-left lanes work together?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: All-way stops run by arrival with right-side ties, protected green arrows stop oncoming yet still want caution, and center lanes serve slowing lefts while far-left lanes serve passing.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: What duties and details come from route guide signs, railroad advance warnings, track-count crossbucks, and crossing emergency notification signs?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.memory_hook: Never race trains, check track count
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: Guide signs orient strangers, rail advance signs warn within a few hundred feet to slow, ready a stop, and never race trains, crossbucks stand at every crossing showing track counts with slow-look-listen yielding, and emergency notification signs carry railroad numbers plus national inventory numbers pinpointing crossings.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: What do litter barrel notices, route shields, interstate mileposts, spurs or business routes, and overhead red-cross, yellow-cross, and green-arrow lane signals tell you?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: More guides point litter barrels a mile ahead and at rest areas, Texas and interstate markers name roads, overhead arrows assign route lanes, interstate mileposts pace emergencies every mile, exit-ahead lanes, short urban state highways, business branches, distance boards, and lane-use signals where red crosses close lanes, steady yellow crosses warn of lane-control changes, and green arrows open lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: How do advance railroad signs and crossbucks differ in placement, and how do overhead red crosses and green arrows control lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: Advance rail signs warn hundreds of feet out, crossbucks mark every crossing with track counts, red crosses close lanes, and green arrows open them.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: When do lowering rail gates and warnings demand stops, and what rules govern two-lane broken lines, one-way lanes, double yellows, and center turn lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.memory_hook: Stop first flash, center turns only
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: Gates demand stops at first flash before lowering and holds until raising with dark lights, rail stops land fifteen to fifty feet out on flaggers, red flashers with bells, or any train warnings, and markings show two-lane rural right-of-center discipline with broken-line passing only, free one-way lane choice with early turn positioning, center lanes entered solely to slow or stop for safe lefts, multi-lane double-yellow respect with slower-right habits, and center lanes never for passing or through travel.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: How do broken lines and solid yellow lines control passing, and what distance window governs railroad crossing stops?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: Broken lines permit safe passing, solid yellow forbids it, and rail stops land fifteen to fifty feet from the rails.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: What do driver-side solid yellow, broken lines, crosswalks, white stop lines, left-edge freeway yellow, single solid white, and double solid white lines mean?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.memory_hook: Solid yellow left, double white bans
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Solid yellow lines on the driver's side ban passing while broken lines allow safe passes and lane changes, white crosswalks define walker zones with stops ahead of them when signs, signals, or walkers require, white stop lines demand stops behind them, solid white edges and channelizers discourage crossing, left-edge interstate yellow forbids leftward travel, and double solid white forbids all crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.front: What job do painted crosswalks and stop lines share, and how does a single solid white line differ from a double solid white line?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.expected_back: Crosswalks and stop lines fix where stops land, solid white discourages crossing, and double solid white bans it outright.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: What do crash barrels, hearing-impaired flags on bikes or cars, and orange diamond or rectangular work-zone devices mean, and when do construction fines double?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.memory_hook: Orange work zone, workers double fines
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: Impact-cushion barrels lessen crash severity near solid obstacles or frequent-crash areas. Slow for a hearing-impaired flag on a bicycle; on a motor vehicle it alerts others. Orange is the basic work-zone-device color. Expect signs, barricades, panels, drums, cones, tubes, arrow panels and flaggers; prepare to reduce speed or stop, change lanes and react to workers or equipment. Most work signs are diamonds, with some rectangles. Traffic fines double for construction-zone violations when workers are present.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.front: What basic color identifies Texas work-zone traffic devices, and under what condition do construction-zone fines double?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.expected_back: Work-zone traffic devices use orange as their basic color. A traffic violation in a construction zone carries double fines when workers are present.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: How must you drive past lit channelizers, sloping barricade stripes, arrow panels, orange-clad flaggers, and remote auto-flagger or pilot-car setups?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.memory_hook: Pass downward stripes, hold for flagger
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: Channelizing devices with night lights order slowing, safe lane changes, late-merger wariness, reduced speed to the zone-end sign, and checked returns, barricade stripes point the passing side by downward slope, arrow panels day and night assign lanes past closures, orange-clad flaggers with paddles and flags command in-lane stops without veering and motionless waits, and remote auto-flaggers plus pilot cars, warnings, and temp signals may assist.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.front: How do diagonal barricade stripes show which side to pass on, and how must you stop and wait for a work-zone flagger?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.expected_back: Stripe slopes point the passing side, and flaggers demand in-lane stops with motionless waits for their signal.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: How do penalties escalate for ignoring warning signs or driving past flooded-road barricades, and which machines may display a slow-moving vehicle emblem?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.memory_hook: Flooded barricade jail, emblem twenty-five max
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: Defying warning signs, markings, or barricades is a misdemeanor fining one to two hundred dollars, doubled in staffed work zones and rising to Class B up to two thousand dollars and one hundred eighty days in jail at flooded roads, while slow-moving emblems belong solely on machines capped at twenty-five miles per hour including animal-drawn rigs, never elsewhere or on fixed objects, except in-zone construction machines and towed implements trailing emblemed movers.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: Which six maneuvers require a signal, how may you give it day or night, how early do you start, and why cancel right after?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Drivers signal every lane change, turn, curb pull-out, slowdown or stop, highway entry or exit, and roadside pull-over, using lamps or bold hand-and-arm gestures from the window, keeping lamps working for darkness, pumping brakes to flag stops, signaling a full one hundred feet ahead, and canceling promptly since stray signals still read as turns.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: Which everyday moves require signaling, how far ahead must your signal run before turning or stopping, and what comes right after turning?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: Use a signal for lane changes, turns, departures from parallel parking, slowing or stopping, highway entry or exit, and pulling to the roadside. Before turning or stopping, keep the signal on for at least one hundred feet; switch off the turn signal after finishing the turn.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: Where is driving on the left half of the road banned, and what three exceptions let you leave the right side?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: The left side stays forbidden under no-passing markings or signs, with two or more lanes each way, within one hundred feet of intersections, rail crossings, bridges, viaducts, and tunnels, and on hills, curves, and blind spots, while drivers otherwise hug the right except to pass on two- or three-lane streets, on one-way roads, or past blocked right sides.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: Within one hundred feet of which structures and crossings is the left side off-limits, and when may you legally leave the right?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: Stay off the road's left side wherever signs or paint forbid it, where traffic has at least two lanes each way, within one hundred feet of or across a junction or rail crossing, on restricted-view hills or bends, and within one hundred feet of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel. The stated keep-right exceptions are overtaking on a two- or three-lane street, one-way travel, or a blocked right side.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: What four habits keep a pass safe, and what crash risk makes impatient passing so dangerous?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: Safe passing waits for clear road, signals lane changes, taps horns against surprises, and returns gently, since botched passes turn head-on and deadly.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: How do you warn a driver before overtaking when needed, and how should you merge back into the lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Overtake only with a clear path, signal before moving between lanes, sound a brief horn warning when needed to avoid surprising the driver ahead, and avoid returning too close in front. Bad passing can cause fatal head-on collisions.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: What steps take you through a two-lane pass from initial checks to canceling your right signal, including oncoming and mirror cues?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: Two-lane passes open with following distance, mirror and blind-spot checks, and a left signal, continue past no-passing checks with enough room to regain the right before oncoming traffic closes inside two hundred feet plus a warning horn tap, and close by passing left, waiting for the overtaken car in the mirror, then signaling right and canceling.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: What oncoming clearance must you keep when passing, and what visual cue tells you it is safe to pull back right?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: Overtakers need oncoming traffic beyond two hundred feet before starting, and the passed car visible in the mirror before returning.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: Under what road or shoulder conditions may you legally pass on the right in Texas, and what surface rule never bends?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Right-side passing is lawful only when safe on clear wide multi-lane roads, on one-way roads, or along paved shoulders past slowing, stopped, disabled, or left-turning vehicles, and never by leaving the pavement.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: Which four vehicle situations let you pass on a paved shoulder, and what road setups allow normal right-side passing?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: Passing on the right requires safe conditions: a road clear of parked vehicles and other obstructions with room for at least two lanes each way, or a one-way road. A paved shoulder may be used to pass a vehicle slowing or stopped in the highway's traveled area, disabled, or about to turn left. Stay on the pavement.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: How must you respond when another driver overtakes you, and what two choices keep an overtaker out of blind spots?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: Passed drivers hold speed and lane, ease right on unmarked lanes, and smooth the passer's path, while passers never linger in blind spots but either complete the pass or fall back out of sight.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: What speed and lane rules bind a driver being overtaken, including on unmarked roads, and how must passers treat blind spots?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: A driver being overtaken must not speed up and must remain in the same lane. If overtaken on the left where lanes are unmarked, shift safely as far right as possible. When overtaking, clear the other driver's blind spot by completing the pass or dropping back.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: How early must you reach your turn lane, what checks come first, and what should you do if you are within half a block?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: Turns start with early decisions against last-second swerves, all-around looks before lane moves, and quick proper-lane entries, skipping any turn missed within half a block.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: How do you manage hand signals, braking, clutching, steering hands, and lane tracking right before and during a turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: Turns continue with signals one hundred feet out, hand signals dropped near the corner for two-handed steering, reasonable pre-turn speed without mid-turn braking or clutching, lane discipline through the maneuver, and proper-lane finishes.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: What is the half-block lane rule, the turn-signal distance rule, and the hand-signal timing rule at an intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: Check behind and on both sides before changing lanes for a turn. Choose the proper lane early; if you cannot reach it at least half a block before the turn, continue straight. Give the turn signal at least one hundred feet ahead. A hand signal should show your intent before the junction, then end for the turn so both hands can steer.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: From lane entry to exit, what are the exact steps and path for making a clean right turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: Right turns stage early lane signals into the far-right lane, add right signals with slowing one hundred feet out, check both ways, hug the right edge, and steer two-handed.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: How do you stage, yield, and track relative to the center point when turning left on two-way streets, and which lane do you enter?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: Left turns stage early signals into the center lane, add left signals with slowing one hundred feet out, scan every direction, stay right of center entering while yielding to oncoming traffic, exit right of center into the least-blocking lane, and change lanes afterward as needed.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: How does your corner path and yielding duty on a right turn contrast with a two-way left turn?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Right turns hug the right edge throughout, while left turns yield oncoming traffic and exit right of center into open lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: When turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street, which lane do you leave and which lane do you enter?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: Lefts from one-way streets onto two-way streets run from the left lane into the same-direction right lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: Which lane should you enter when turning left onto a one-way street, and what overrides standard single-lane turn paths?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Lefts onto one-way streets enter the least-blocking lane, and drivers heed markings and signs authorizing multi-lane turns or special lane moves.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: Which signals govern pedestrians at intersections, and where should you wait before crossing?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: Walkers obey traffic signals unless pedestrian signals redirect them, waiting on curbs rather than streets for green or WALK phases.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: Where is crossing banned between intersections, which side of a crosswalk do you use, and when do you look both ways?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Walkers never cross mid-block between intersections, keep right inside crosswalks where possible, and look both ways before crossing and before emerging from behind parked cars.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: How do signal waits, mid-block rules, and crosswalk positioning fit together for pedestrians?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: Signals rule crossings from curb waits, mid-block crossings stay banned, and crosswalks keep right.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: Where must you walk first if available, and what do you do on a road without sidewalks?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: Walkers take sidewalks where they exist, otherwise walk left facing traffic and step off pavement for approaching cars.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: What three-step order decides where a pedestrian walks and reacts to approaching vehicles?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: Sidewalks come first, left-side facing traffic comes without sidewalks, and stepping off comes with traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: Who gets the right-of-way when a pedestrian crosses outside an intersection crosswalk or skips a tunnel or overpass?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Walkers crossing outside intersection crosswalks or bypassing provided tunnels and overpasses yield to every vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: Which two pedestrian shortcuts both require yielding the right-of-way to every vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: Crossing outside crosswalks yields to all vehicles, as does skipping provided tunnels and overpasses.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: Who may carry a white cane on public streets, and when is standing in a roadway to solicit allowed?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: White canes belong solely to blind, partially blind, or disabled walkers on public roads, and nobody stands in roads seeking rides, contributions, or business except locally authorized charitable solicitors.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: Who holds exclusive public-road rights to a white cane, and what sole permission allows roadside fundraising?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: White canes on public streets or highways are reserved for people who are blind, partially blind or disabled. Standing in the road to seek rides, donations or business is prohibited; charitable fundraising is allowed only with permission from the local authority responsible for that road.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: What six safety habits protect pedestrians around traffic, transit stops, car doors, night walks, alcohol, and local crossing bans?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: Walkers never dart into vehicle paths, wear white or light clothes with lights or reflectors at night, step carefully from buses and streetcars, enter and leave cars curbside, avoid walking while drinking since alcohol feeds walker crashes, and heed local bans on business-district and designated-highway crossings outside crosswalks.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: Which three pedestrian rules target sudden street entries, nighttime visibility, and alcohol risk?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: Darting stays banned, night wants light clothes and reflectors, and alcohol stays off walkways.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: What three actions should a driver take upon spotting someone crossing or about to cross the street?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: Drivers spotting crossing or attempting walkers slow, sound horns when needed, and ready full stops.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: How must drivers respond when a pedestrian with a white cane or assistance animal is crossing or trying to cross?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: Drivers heed assistance animals and white canes marking blind, partially blind, or disabled walkers, take every precaution against harming crossing or attempting walkers, and stop fully whenever only stopping avoids injury or danger.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: How does your duty toward general crossing pedestrians step up when a white cane is present?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: Crossing walkers earn slowed horned readiness, while cane walkers earn precautions up to mandatory full stops.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: At which four locations should drivers stay extra alert for blind pedestrians?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: Drivers watch for blind individuals at bus stops, intersections, business districts, and schools for the blind.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: When behind the wheel, what level of attention do you owe people on foot?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: Drivers always pay special attention to persons on foot.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: What four habits and legal duties define a defensive driver in Texas?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: Defensive drivers stay alert with roaming eyes, spot brewing trouble early, hold a response plan, and honor the legal duty to shield others from their own errors.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: Who must buckle up in belt-equipped vehicles, which children need car seats, and what three crash dangers do belts prevent?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: All riders in belt-equipped passenger vehicles, pickups, SUVs, and trucks must buckle up, and children under eight need approved car seats unless past four feet nine inches, since belts prevent ejection, dashboard strikes, and lost control.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: How do Texas fine ranges compare across unbelted drivers, riders fifteen and older, small children, riders under seventeen, and open-bed minors?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: Unbelted drivers face fines from twenty-five to fifty dollars, and the same band hits unbelted riders fifteen and up, while unsecured small children draw twenty-five to two hundred fifty, unbelted under-seventeens cost drivers one hundred to two hundred, and open-bed under-eighteens cost drivers twenty-five to two hundred.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: Below what age are passengers barred from open pickup or trailer beds, and which six defenses apply?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: Children under eighteen may not ride in open truck or trailer beds, though parades, emergencies, rural farm-worker shuttles, beaches, sole household vehicles, and permitted hayrides defend the charge.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: What three core takeaways sum up Texas seatbelt rules, child safety seats, and fine severity?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: Every seat buckles, small children ride in car seats, and skipped belts cost drivers most for young riders.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: When is towing a boat or personal watercraft with someone under eighteen aboard legal versus an offense?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: Towing a boat or watercraft with a rider under eighteen aboard is an offense, excused only by parade, emergency, or beach operation.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: What criminal classification applies to riding inside a towed trailer or semitrailer, and which exceptions excuse it?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: Occupying a towed trailer or semitrailer is a Class B misdemeanor unless the tower was unaware, the space suits habitation, or the trip was a parade, emergency, farm shuttle, or permitted hayride.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: What pattern links the passenger bans and common exceptions across open truck beds, towed boats, and towed trailers?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: Open beds, towed boats, and towed trailers each bar young or all riders, with parades and emergencies excusing most cases.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: Which six vehicle steps should you complete as soon as an officer signals you to pull over?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: When signaled to stop, drivers pull fully right, park clear of traffic, engage parking gear and brake, shut off the engine, flash hazards, and light the dome lamp after dark.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: Once parked for a traffic stop, how should you handle your hands, window, passengers, weapons, documents, and departure?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: Stopped drivers stay seated with both hands on the wheel, crack the window when safe, take orders from either side, declare weapons, announce document locations before reaching, exit only when told, hold passengers inside, and signal out when released.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: Which three courtesy practices keep a roadside stop calm around seating, hand movement, and handgun storage?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: Courtesy keeps everyone seated unless summoned, hands still until the officer nears, and handguns stored away from licenses and insurance.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: What three core actions anchor safe parking, hand placement, and document retrieval during a police stop?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: Stops park right and dark, hands stay on the wheel, and papers wait for permission.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: What must you normally do for emergency lights behind you, and what three steps apply if the spot feels unsafe?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: Drivers must halt at once for emergency vehicles or risk arrest, though where stopping feels unsafe they may crawl with hazards lit, phone emergency dispatch while complying, or continue to a lighted public spot.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: How does Texas balance immediate stops for police lights with personal safety on dark, isolated stretches?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: Emergency lights demand instant halts, yet scary spots allow hazard-lit crawls to safety.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: During a traffic stop or arrest, when does the right to silence apply, and what identification must you provide truthfully?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: Stops are short investigative detentions where silence is protected yet licenses must be shown, arrestees must state name, address, and birth date, and false identities or answers invite arrest.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: Can you decline a vehicle search request, when may an officer search anyway, and how must you respond physically?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: Drivers may refuse vehicle searches, but probable cause or a suspected weapon lets officers search or pat down anyway, and resistance is unlawful even while voicing non-consent.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: How do silence, driver licenses, and vehicle searches each work during a Texas traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: Silence stays free, licenses stay mandatory, and searches need consent unless cause exists.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: What does signing a traffic ticket actually mean, and how should you handle any misconduct complaint?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: Misconduct complaints go to the officer's superiors with agency and badge details, drivers never argue roadside, and a signed citation promises payment or a court date rather than admitting guilt.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: Why should you sign a citation calmly and save any dispute until after the traffic stop ends?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: Signed tickets promise court dates rather than guilt, and grievances travel upward after the stop.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: What makes giving a fake name unlawful, and what two factors escalate the penalty for fleeing an officer?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: Falsely naming oneself during lawful detention is an offense, and fleeing an officer grows worse when wheels or watercraft aid escape or someone is hurt.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: What six calm driving habits help you defuse road rage and deal with aggressive drivers?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: Road rage wounds hundreds yearly, so drivers defuse it by planning routes, breathing through jams, tapping horns, signaling every lane move, refusing to block or tailgate, and reporting aggressors.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: What are the legal and safety stakes for giving a false identity, evading detention, and road rage?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: A person may be arrested for giving a false identity to an officer who lawfully arrests or detains them. Evading arrest or detention brings greater penalties when a vehicle or watercraft is used or another person is injured. Road rage causes hundreds of injuries and deaths annually.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: Which federal safety standard must a neighborhood electric vehicle meet, and what is its top flat-pavement speed?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: Neighborhood electric vehicles meet Federal Motor Safety Standard five hundred and cap at thirty-five miles per hour on flat pavement.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: What five mechanical features define a legal motor-assisted scooter in Texas?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: Motor-assisted scooters carry at least two grounded wheels, reliable brakes, a forty-cc-or-smaller motor, a stand-or-sit deck, and human-power backup.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: Up to what posted speed limits may neighborhood electric vehicles and motor-assisted scooters operate, and who can ban them?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: Neighborhood electrics run only where limits read forty-five or less and scooters where they read thirty-five or less, and local governments may bar either for safety.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: How is a self-balancing assistive device built, and when and where may it use sidewalks, paths, or residential streets?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: Segway-style assistive devices balance one rider on two side-by-side wheels near seven hundred fifty watts, and may use sidewalks, bike paths, and slow residential streets only to cross, cover sidewalk gaps, or obey direction, hugging the right edge on roadways.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: What separates neighborhood electric vehicles, motor-assisted scooters, and self-balancing devices under Texas law?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: Neighborhood electrics, scooters, and balancing devices each cap speed and street access differently.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: Which six everyday habits make up the handbook's keys to safe driving?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: Safe-driving keys span clear vision, law obedience, maintained cars, courtesy above right-of-way, faithful signals, and driving only when fit.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: How must truck cargo beds and tie-downs secure loads, and when do loose dirt-type loads require a tarp?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: Cargo beds must be solid, sided, front-closed, and rear-gated with loads tied front and back, while loose dirt-class freight needs boxed beds plus lashed tarps unless fully enclosed or riding below the rails.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: Which vehicles must connect DPS-approved safety chains when pulling a trailer, and which two setups are exempt?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: Cars and light trucks towing trailers must hitch DPS-approved safety chains, excepting farm trailers and federally compliant rigs.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: What length, strength, flag size, vehicle count, and cargo exception apply to tow links and bars?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: Tow links run fifteen feet or less, hold the full weight, show a twelve-inch-square white flag, and drag at most three front-lifted vehicles, save pole and pipe hauls.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: How do Texas hauling laws lock down loose cargo, light-duty trailers, and tow connections?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: Loads stay boxed and tarped, trailers stay chained, and tow bars stay short and flagged.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: Which five habits prevent carbon monoxide poisoning around vehicles, and what two steps help a victim?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: Carbon monoxide kills quietly, so drivers never idle in garages, trail traffic with open vents, idle sealed cars, drive on broken exhausts, or heat parked cars indoors, and they drag victims to fresh air and call nine one one.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.front: Why is vehicle exhaust called a silent threat, what does it forbid, and what is first aid for exposure?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.expected_back: Silent exhaust gas forbids indoor idling and broken mufflers, and victims need fresh air fast.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: Which two optional forms let Texans with communication challenges add a driver license code and a vehicle registration alert?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: Texans with communication challenges may add an optional license code with physician-signed form DL-one hundred one and flag vehicle registrations with form VTR-two hundred sixteen so dispatch alerts officers before they approach.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.front: How do Texas's optional communication indicators protect drivers and passengers during a roadside stop?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.expected_back: Communication barriers earn optional license and registration flags that warn officers early.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: Who needs a Texas driver license, and how do the rules treat ninety-day newcomers, non-farm machines, sixteen-plus or eighteen-plus nonresidents, and military members?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: Texas licenses cover residents, ninety-day new residents, non-farm commercial-free machines, sixteen-plus nonresidents for Class C or M, eighteen-plus nonresidents for anything with home reciprocity, and military drivers on home licenses with Texas cards surviving service plus ninety days.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: How does the Texas ninety-day license clock for new residents differ from the rule for active-duty military drivers?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.memory_hook: Newcomers ninety days, service plus ninety
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: New residents face a ninety-day clock to qualify for a Texas license, while service members keep an existing Texas card valid through duty plus ninety days after.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: Who must ride beside a Texas learner driver, who can apply, what do teen versus restricted adult cards cost, and what happens to old cards?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: Learner driving needs a sober watchful companion twenty-one plus with a year of experience, applicants run fifteen to eighteen with classroom education and exams passed, cards cost sixteen dollars total to age eighteen, practicing adults pay thirty-three dollars total for eight restricted years, and all prior cards surrender first.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: How do the total price and expiration window compare between a teen learner card and a practicing adult's restricted license?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: A learner card costs sixteen dollars total and ends at eighteen, while a practicing adult pays thirty-three dollars total for eight restricted years.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: If you are under eighteen applying for the first time, what attendance or diploma benchmarks must your school VOE show, and how fresh must it be?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: Under-eighteen first-timers file a school VOE proving a diploma, eighty prior-term days, or forty-five equivalency-prep days, fresh within thirty days in session or ninety in summer.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: How long does a signed school VOE stay valid during the school year versus during summer break?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: A school VOE stays fresh thirty days in session but ninety days across summer.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: How can a fifteen- to eighteen-year-old qualify for a hardship license, and what exam and hold rules govern Texas graduated licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.memory_hook: Proven crisis petition, six learner months
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: Hardship licenses aid fifteen- to eighteen-year-olds via in-person adult petitions, full education and exams, and approval only for money crisis, family emergency, vocational need, or court order, inside a graduated system forcing driving exams on all newcomers, six learner months stretched by suspensions, and no Phase One wait for Class M.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: What separates qualifying for a hardship license from completing graduated Phase One?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: Hardship approval turns on proven need and narrow grounds, while graduated Phase One turns on a six-month learner hold that suspensions stretch.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: Once you reach Phase Two of graduated licensing, what three limits restrict passengers, overnight driving, and wireless devices?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.memory_hook: One young peer, curfew, no wireless
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: Phase Two caps young non-family passengers at one, bans midnight-to-five driving outside work, school, or emergency, and forbids under-eighteen wireless use beyond emergencies.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: In graduated Phase Two, how do the young-passenger cap and the midnight-to-five curfew apply independently?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: Phase Two caps young non-family riders at one and separately bans midnight-to-five driving outside work, school, or emergency.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: Who gets PROVISIONAL or UNDER twenty-one cards, how do out-of-state teens place in GDL, how long do adult cards run, and what about commercial-exempt rigs?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.memory_hook: Provisional to eighteen, adults eight years
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: PROVISIONAL cards run sixteen to eighteen after education, exams, and six learner months, out-of-state teens sort into Phase One or Two by credential, under-twenty-one cards read UNDER twenty-one, adult licenses run eight years for thirty-three dollars total with shorter special terms, and eight commercial-exempt vehicle types still need Class A or B.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: How does the age range for a PROVISIONAL marking differ from an UNDER twenty-one marking on a Texas license?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: PROVISIONAL marks sixteen- to eighteen-year-old license holders, while UNDER twenty-one marks every card issued before twenty-one.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: What vehicles and trailer weights do non-commercial Class A and Class B licenses cover, do they cover motorcycles, and what do they cost?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.memory_hook: Class A combinations, B heavy singles
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: Class A spans B and C vehicles plus heavy combinations towing over ten thousand pounds and Class B spans C vehicles plus heavy singles towing ten thousand or twenty-thousand-pound farm trailers, neither touching motorcycles, each thirty-three dollars total for eight adult years with education through twenty-four or sixteen dollars total at seventeen with education.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: How does the weight test for needing a Class A license differ from the weight test for Class B?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: Class A combinations are judged by combined weight with heavy towed weight, while Class B singles are judged by single-vehicle weight with lighter towing caps.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: What vehicles and three fee tiers belong to Class C, and what course or teen credentials are required for Class M?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.memory_hook: Cars and autocycles, course for bikes
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: Class C covers lighter vehicles, small trailers and certified three-wheel autocycles, never motorcycles. Listed totals are thirty-three dollars for adults, sixteen dollars at sixteen with approved driver education, or six dollars at fifteen with hardship approval. Class M requires passing a state-approved motorcycle course; under-eighteen enrollees may show classroom-phase completion, a learner license or a valid Class C license as alternatives.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: What are the three total dollar prices for a Texas Class C license across adult, educated-teen, and hardship paths?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.memory_hook: Thirty-three adult, sixteen teen, six hardship
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: Class C prices split three ways by path, thirty-three dollars total as an adult, sixteen dollars total at sixteen with education, or six dollars total at fifteen with hardship.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: At what ages and education hours does motorcycle licensing open, what are the issue, add-on, and renewal fees, and which veterans pay zero?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.memory_hook: Sixteen full bikes, fifteen small bikes
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: Motorcycle licensing opens at sixteen after thirty-two plus sixteen hours or fifteen for small bikes via hardship or courses, charging thirty-three dollars total adult, sixteen dollars total young, sixteen to append, and twelve extra at renewal, with sixty-percent-plus disabled veterans skipping fees outside commercial and registrant cases.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: How does the fee to append Class M onto an active license compare with the extra fee when renewing Class M?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.memory_hook: Sixteen to add, twelve to renew
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: Appending M to a live license costs sixteen dollars total, while renewing M adds twelve dollars total on top of renewal.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: Who can get a Texas ID card, how is it oriented and priced by age, and how do emergency contacts or allergy drugs go on the back?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.memory_hook: Any age ID, handwrite allergy meds
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: ID cards issue at any age, orient vertical under twenty-one, cost sixteen dollars total for six years through fifty-nine or six dollars total later, and backs allow two emergency contacts with allergy drugs handwritten since DPS prints no medical facts.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: What does the heart donor mark establish, which five causes can applicants fund, and how do voter offers and Selective Service work at DPS?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.memory_hook: Heart binds consent, selective service automatic
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: Donor cards show a heart plus donor as conclusive consent, applicants may fund blindness care, Donate Life, veterans, evidence testing, or youth fees, filing happens in person with voter offers from seventeen years ten months, and men eighteen to twenty-five join selective service automatically.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: How does the legal meaning of the donor heart on your card differ from the five contribution checkboxes on the application?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.memory_hook: Heart binds gift, checkboxes donate cash
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: The donor heart on the card front is binding consent for gifts, while the five contribution checkboxes are optional donations.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: What identity, biometric, insurance, and prior-card steps apply when filing, and which events stay on your permanent driving record?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: Applicants provide identity, Social Security number, fingerprints, medical-status and history answers and citizenship or lawful-presence proof, and surrender any valid out-of-state license. Exams, moving-traffic convictions and crashes enter the permanent record. Original applicants show Texas-minimum insurance for owned vehicles needing coverage, or state that none require it.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: What vehicle-registration, fee, driver-education, Impact Texas Drivers, and guardian-signature rules apply before you sit for exams?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.memory_hook: Register, pay, finish Impact Texas first
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: New residents register all owned vehicles, fees with a one-dollar admin charge precede exams with none by mail, under-twenty-five drivers finish education, everyone finishes Impact Texas Drivers pre-exam, and under-eighteen filings carry a guardian oath signature cancellable before eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: How long do failed applications sit, what temporary card do passers earn, what score passes knowledge tests, and what can vision checks require?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: Failures park applications ninety days, valid-license adults skip exams, passers earn forty-five-day temporary cards, knowledge exams span Class C originals, waivable Class M, and Class A and B rules with seventy percent passing all, and vision checks can mandate lenses or doctor visits.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: How does the ninety-day clock after failing exams compare with the forty-five-day window after passing?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.memory_hook: Fail parks ninety, pass gets forty-five
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: Exam failure parks an application ninety days, while exam success earns a forty-five-day temporary card.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: Across Class C, Class M, and Class A or B knowledge exams, what minimum score is needed to pass?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.memory_hook: Every knowledge test needs seventy percent
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: Class C, Class M, and Class A and B exams each test different drivers, yet every one passes at seventy percent or better.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: When and where do driving tests run, who can never waive them, what do upgrades cost, and what triggers a road-test fail?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: Driving exams follow passed exams and proven insurance in class-matched vehicles, excuse nobody under eighteen, run at offices and schools, skip learners, cost ten dollars to upgrade or fifteen to append M, and fail lawbreakers, the disobedient, the dangerous, and anyone beyond thirty lost points.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.front: What does it cost to step up a class or drop restrictions versus adding Class M, and how many lost points fail an exam?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.memory_hook: Ten upgrade, fifteen bike, thirty points
sec01-card-sec01-R13.expected_back: Stepping up a class or shedding restrictions costs ten dollars, appending Class M costs fifteen dollars, and any exam fails past thirty lost points.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Which driving skills and habits get graded during the road exam, and how are backup cameras treated compared with automated parking?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: Grading covers control, observation, positioning, signaling, parking, quick stops, backing, signs, signals, clutch, intersections, turns, right-of-way, following, passing, lanes, and posture, allowing cameras while banning automated parking.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: Who can demand to see your license, where can restrictions be changed, and what fines or jail apply for driving unlicensed?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.memory_hook: Carry always, unlicensed penalties escalate fast
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: Failed exams reschedule, passers carry the license for officers and crash counterparts, unlicensed fines run two hundred dollars first and twenty-five to two hundred second within a year or Class A jail for deadly uninsured crashes, and restrictions change at any office.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.front: How do Texas unlicensed-driving penalties climb from a first conviction to a repeat within one year and a deadly uninsured crash?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.memory_hook: Two hundred first, Class A deadly
sec01-card-sec01-R14.expected_back: Unlicensed fines rise from two hundred dollars first to a twenty-five-to-two-hundred-dollar band on a second within a year, then leap to Class A jail for deadly uninsured crashes.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: How soon must you report an address move, what do updates or duplicates cost, and does a missing renewal notice excuse driving expired?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.memory_hook: Report moves thirty days, eleven dollars
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: Duplicates and address moves cost eleven dollars total with thirty-day reporting, ten dollars by mail, other changes in person, no remote service for special licenses, and renewal notices stay pure courtesy.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: How often do licenses renew versus require office visits, who is barred from remote renewal, and how do military or out-of-state renewals work?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.memory_hook: Renew every eight, visit every sixteen
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: Renewal runs eight years with office visits each sixteen for vision and biometrics, remote service bars troubled, commercial, restricted, registrant, older, undocumented, and non-citizen filers, medical answers may reach the board, service families renew exam-free within ninety days of discharge, and out-of-state Texans mail fees and vision results to the printed date or ninety days after return.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.front: How does the eight-year license renewal cycle pair up with Texas's mandatory in-person appearance cycle?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.expected_back: Licenses renew every eight years, yet every driver still appears in person at least each sixteen years for vision and biometrics.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: What reinstatement fees and SR-twenty-two rules apply after mandatory or ALR actions, and which four intoxication or drug offenses trigger automatic suspension?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: one hundred dollars may be required for mandatory suspensions, revocations and certain fraudulent-government-record convictions; drug-education reinstatement is one hundred dollars. ALR reinstatement is one hundred twenty-five dollars. Some mandatory suspensions need SR-twenty-two. Listed automatic-suspension triggers include DWI, drug offenses, intoxication manslaughter and intoxication assault.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: Besides DWI and drug convictions, what twelve other acts — including street racing, boating intoxication, card fraud, or graffiti — automatically suspend a license?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: Automatic suspension adds aid failures, deadly crashes, felonies, bus repeats, boating intoxication, evading, invalid driving, card fraud, graffiti, fake plates, false records, and racing.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: Which conviction counts or compliance failures trigger a suspension hearing, and what substance offenses automatically suspend drivers under twenty-one?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.memory_hook: Ticket streaks trigger hearings, youth substances
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: Hearings suspend for bad patterns of four convictions in twelve months or seven in twenty-four plus exam and probation failures, and under-twenty-one drivers fall automatically for alcohol, tobacco-class, drug, and Chapter four eighty-one offenses.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.front: How many moving-traffic convictions trigger a suspension hearing within twelve months versus within twenty-four months?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.memory_hook: Four in twelve, seven in twenty-four
sec01-card-sec01-R16.expected_back: Hearing review follows four convictions in twelve months but needs seven in twenty-four.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: What rules govern a minor's two-ticket hearing, delinquent-conduct suspension, ALR chemical-test triggers and fee, and license cancellation grounds?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.memory_hook: Two teen tickets, refusal, detectable alcohol
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: After a proper hearing, a minor may face suspension or revocation for a juvenile court order, unpaid fine or juvenile contempt, or at least two separate traffic convictions within twelve months while under eighteen. Delinquent conduct falls under automatic suspension for those under twenty-one. ALR reinstatement costs one hundred twenty-five dollars; triggers include a failed breath or blood test at point zero eight or above for persons over twenty-one, refusing a test, or detectable alcohol under twenty-one. Cancellation grounds include another state's suspension or revocation, withdrawn parental approval under eighteen, missing required information, ineligibility, incomplete driver education, or false application statements.

sec01-card-sec01-R17.front: How does the alcohol trigger for license revocation differ between drivers twenty-one and up versus drivers under twenty-one?
sec01-card-sec01-R17.memory_hook: Adults point zero eight, minors any
sec01-card-sec01-R17.expected_back: Revocation starts at point zero eight for twenty-one-plus drivers but at any detectable alcohol under twenty-one.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: Which six court orders force mandatory restrictions, freezes, or action against a Texas driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.memory_hook: Support, interlock, incapacity, lapsed annual renewal
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: Court orders compel action for child support, interlock, overpayments, incapacity, dependency, or lapsed annual renewal.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: What offenses, conditions, or debts block license issuance or renewal, and how do penalties escalate for driving while invalid?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.memory_hook: Missed court blocks renewal, invalid climbs
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: Denials track live disqualifications, unsafe conditions, theft, mischief, minor alcohol supply, support debt, unpaid fees, missed court, and drugs, while invalid driving scales from Class C fines through Class B jail to Class A jail with extensions, and skipped traffic court can block renewal.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: What does Zero Tolerance forbid for minors, and what fines, service hours, and suspension days hit first, second, and third offenses?

sec01-card-sec01-R18.front: How do Zero Tolerance license suspension lengths climb across first, second, and older-teen third offenses?
sec01-card-sec01-R18.memory_hook: Thirty days, sixty, then one eighty

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: What maximum fine and jail time face someone convicted of supplying alcohol to a minor in Texas?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.memory_hook: Four thousand fine, one year jail
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: Supplying alcohol to a minor risks four thousand dollars, a year in jail, or both.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: How do you qualify for an occupational license, what does it cost, what papers must ride in the car, and does it cover commercial trucks?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.memory_hook: Essential court order, never commercial rigs
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: Court-proved essential need buys occupational licenses at ten dollars yearly or twenty for two, the order alone covering forty-five processing days before both order and certified copy ride along, never for commercial rigs.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: When must your headlights stay on in Texas, how fast may you drive at night, and where should your eyes look against oncoming glare?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Night driving runs far deadlier with weaker sight, so daylight trips beat night runs and tired drivers stay parked, night speeds drop inside headlight range, lamps burn from thirty minutes after sunset to thirty minutes before sunrise or under one-thousand-foot visibility, and eyes shift low-right against oncoming glare.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: At what distances from other cars and in which road or weather conditions must you switch to low beams — plus what lights stay on if parked on an unlit highway?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.memory_hook: Five hundred ahead, three hundred behind
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Low beams take over within five hundred feet of oncoming cars, within three hundred feet behind leaders, on lit roads, and in fog, rain, sleet, snow, or dust, while night-parked cars on dark highways keep parking or low beams lit.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: What are the exact time, visibility, oncoming, and following numbers for turning headlights on and dipping to low beams?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: Use headlights from a half-hour after sunset to a half-hour before sunrise, or whenever people or vehicles cannot be seen clearly for at least one thousand feet. Use low beams within five hundred feet of an approaching vehicle or when following another vehicle within three hundred feet.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: How does Texas define a highway, how should you plan before entering one, and how do you merge from the entrance lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Texas highways span the maintained public width between boundary lines, trips pre-plan entrances, directions, and exits with fit drivers and cars skipping roads above their minimum pace, and entries yield to highway traffic through right-side speed-change lanes with left signals and merging speed.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: What four actions take you smoothly onto a Texas highway from the entrance ramp?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: Highway entries yield to flow, ride right-side speed lanes, signal left, and accelerate into merges.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: How are right, middle, and left freeway lanes assigned, what following gaps apply in dry versus bad weather, and how should you treat faster or merging cars?

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: How far ahead are freeway exit signs usually posted, when should you move into the exit lane, and where do you slow down?

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: Which freeway lanes match slower versus faster traffic, and how far in advance do exit signs warn you to get over?

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: How often should you stop on long trips, what is the daily driving cap, how do you stay alert on the highway, and what cell-phone rule applies under eighteen?

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: What are the four core numbers for dry gaps, bad-weather gaps, rest breaks, and maximum daily highway hours?

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: If your car breaks down, what should happen with passengers, getting off the pavement, lighting up at night, and signaling for help?

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: In what exact four-step priority order does Texas say to secure a roadside breakdown?

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: What golden rule governs emergencies, how do you recover from a skid without making it worse, and what prevents skids beforehand?

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: How do you safely handle brake failure, dropping off the pavement edge, a tire blowout, and driving down a steep hill?

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: Across skids, failed brakes, pavement drop-offs, and blowouts, what one panic mistake must you avoid every single time?

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: Why is there no safe speed on ice, where does ice form or linger longest, and how much grip do snow tires or chains really buy?

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: How many conflict points do roundabouts cut compared with four-way signals, how do you navigate single or multi-lane circles, and where do you pull over for sirens?

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: What four rules take you cleanly into, around, and out of a roundabout — even when an emergency siren approaches?

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: What happens to vehicles at six inches, twelve inches, and two feet of floodwater, what if your car stalls in water, and how much do roundabouts cut severe crashes?

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: Which three water depths steal car control, float passenger cars, and sweep away pickups or SUVs?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.memory_hook: Six inches, twelve inches, two feet

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: How much extra time should you budget to pass a large truck on level ground, how do hills change it, and when is it safe to pull back in front?

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: What extra time and two clearance signals govern passing a large truck and returning to your lane?

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: How do car and loaded-truck stopping distances compare at fifty-five miles per hour, what does wind turbulence do when meeting a rig, and how should you stop behind one uphill?
