sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: Passed drivers drift far-side, ease speed, never accelerate, and heed truck return signals, oncoming meetings hug far sides against sideswipes since turbulence pushes apart, following respects two-hundred-forty-foot car stops against four-hundred-plus-foot loaded rig stops at fifty-five miles per hour, rear blind spots stay empty with drivers visible in truck side mirrors, night lights dim against mirror glare, and uphill stops leave rollback room on the left for visibility.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: What are the car versus loaded-rig stopping distances, the side-mirror visibility rule, and the direction air turbulence pushes?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.memory_hook: Four hundred plus, air pushes apart
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: Cars stop near two hundred forty feet while loaded rigs need four hundred plus, unseen drivers mean unseen cars, and turbulence pushes apart.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: Why must you never squeeze to the right of a turning truck, rush past a backing rig, cut into a truck's front gap, or trust how slow an approaching rig looks?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.memory_hook: Never squeeze right, protect front cushion
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Truck right turns swing wide past deceptive right-side gaps that passing cars must avoid, backing trucks block roads that waiting cars must respect from outside blind spots, center-lane cruising aids merges and escape options, cutoffs steal safety cushions with construction-zone races worst of all, and big size masks true truck speed at intersections.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: How much more likely are motorcyclists to die in crashes, why do drivers miss seeing them, and which car maneuver causes the deadliest collisions?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.memory_hook: Thirty-five times deadlier, watch left turns
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: Motorcyclists share full road rights, yet half of bike crashes involve other vehicles and riders die about thirty-five times more often, hidden by car-seeking eyes, tiny profiles, tricky distance judgment, constant lane shifts, and distraction, with left turns across their path most deadly plus blind spots, surface hazards, wind gusts, and large-vehicle blocking.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: Why can you never trust a motorcycle's flashing turn signal alone, and how much lane width does a rider get?

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: What is the number-one car-versus-motorcycle crash, and which three habits protect riders around your car?

Motorcyclists are often hidden in blind spots; check mirrors and blind spots before lane changes and at intersections, signal before changing lanes or merging, and allow a motorcycle its full lane width.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: What following and stopping cushions do motorcycles need, what shifted in twenty twenty for Texas rider training, and how must you behave around light-rail tracks?

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: When may a bicyclist legally take a full lane or ride outside the right edge, how should you make a right turn near a cyclist, and which three crashes hit riders most?

sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: Bicycles count as vehicles with full rights and duties, ride beyond right lanes on one-way multi-lane streets and car-pathed left turns, earn motorist merges on right turns without cut-across moves, hug right only in safely shareable lanes, claim full lanes to pass, turn left, dodge hazards, or survive narrow lanes, and crash most when cars left-hook oncoming riders, right-hook their paths, or pull from stops across their right-of-way.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: What three things does distraction pull away from driving, how much does a half-second delay spike crash risk, how do you prep before rolling, and how do you handle distracted drivers nearby?

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: How does Texas treat right-of-way when another driver ignores the rules, and what fine ranges hit failure-to-yield crashes causing bodily or serious bodily injury?

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: Beyond obeying intersection signs and signals, which road yields when a one- or two-lane road meets a larger road, or unpaved meets paved?

sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: Narrow roads yield to divided or three-plus-lane roads, while unpaved roads yield to paved ones.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: Who yields or stops at uncontrolled intersections, during left turns, when exiting a private driveway or alley, and on the ending street of a T-intersection?

sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: At uncontrolled crossings drivers yield to the right and proceed only when the right runs clear or distant while still checking left, left turns yield to straight-through oncoming traffic, private entries stop ahead of the sidewalk for all vehicles and walkers, and T-intersection endings stop for the through street.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: How do your stopping and yielding duties compare across an oncoming left turn, the ending leg of a T-intersection, and a private driveway exit?

At a T-intersection, traffic on the ending street stops and yields to vehicles on the through street. Leaving a private road, alley, building or driveway requires stopping before the sidewalk and yielding to all approaching vehicles and pedestrians.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: Who yields on Texas frontage roads and same-direction multi-lane merges, how far from railroad tracks must you stop, and which warnings trigger that stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: Frontage-road drivers yield to vehicles entering or leaving the highway, same-direction multi-lane entries from the right yield to entries from the left, and rail crossings demand a stop fifteen to fifty feet from the nearest rail on signals, gates, flags, devices, trains within about one thousand five hundred feet, audible warnings, or close visible trains.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: Rail stops land fifteen to fifty feet from the rails, triggered by warnings or trains within about one thousand five hundred feet.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: What fine backs rail-crossing stops, how do you handle crossbucks, lights, gates, and clearing tracks, and which way do you flee a stalled car?

sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: Drivers stay stopped at rail crossings until safe under a fifty-to-two-hundred-dollar fine, treat crossbucks with look-and-listen caution, hold through flashing red until trains pass and lights die, hold lowered gates until trains pass and gates rise, clear every track before crossing, never halt on rails, shove or flee stalled cars by running trackside toward the train, grant trains unstoppable priority, and drop windows and radios to hear whistles.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: Flashing red means hold until train and lights finish, lowered gates mean hold until train and gates finish, and stalled drivers flee trackside toward the train.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: Who do you call for a broken railroad crossing signal versus a track emergency, and which numbers from the blue-and-white sign do you report?

sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: Broken crossing signals go to DPS communications or local officers with the crossing's ID number, and emergencies use the blue-and-white notification sign's railroad number plus the national crossing inventory number and the problem's nature.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: How must you clear the road for an approaching emergency vehicle, how far behind lit fire or ambulance runs must you stay, and what is banned near alarms?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: Siren, bell, or red-light emergency vehicles get the road via a right-edge stop or a slowed clear path, followers stay five hundred feet behind lit fire and ambulance runs, and nobody drives, parks, or blocks around answered alarms.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: How is disabled-parking abuse classified, how do fines escalate from first to fifth offense, and do traffic-sign stops count as parking?

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: What five steps are legally required before leaving a vehicle unattended, and how do remote-start systems fit into that rule?

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: How do you line up and begin backing into a parallel spot, and what is the maximum curb distance on a two-way street?

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: What fines, confinement ranges, and license suspensions apply to adult DWI from first through third offenses, child-passenger cases, assault, and manslaughter?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Driving intoxicated with any passenger younger than fifteen automatically jumps straight past misdemeanors into a ten-thousand-dollar state-jail felony.
sec10-card-sec10-F13.must_match_memory_hook: Two, four, ten thousand, prison climbs

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: How do adult refusal days compare with adult failure days on first and repeat stops, and where do repeat or severe DWI charges lead?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Administrative breath-test suspensions run separately from criminal court sentences, meaning drivers face immediate license loss before trial even starts.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Guessing or abbreviating an insurance carrier's name can stall your repair claim because dozens of Texas companies carry nearly identical titles.
sec11-card-sec11-F01.must_match_memory_hook: Copy insurer and policy number exact

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: Which three driving errors top Texas crash stats, and how carefully must you write down insurance details?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Nearly every preventable collision starts with rushing, rolling past right-of-way rules, or driving impaired, so accurate scene notes protect everyone afterward.
sec11-card-sec11-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Speed, yield, alcohol, copy policy exact

visual_sync.text_span: Speed, yield, alcohol, copy policy exact

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: Which four crash situations require notifying law enforcement immediately right from the scene?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Any crash with hurt people, a blocked roadbed, a runaway driver, or suspected impairment needs officers dispatched before evidence disappears.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: When police do not investigate a minor crash without injury, death, or one thousand dollars in damage, what report is needed and by what deadline?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Watch the wording carefully on permit questions because this ten-day transportation form covers minor uninvestigated crashes below the thousand-dollar mark.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: How does Texas split immediate police-call crashes from ten-day written-report crashes?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Knowing whether to dial dispatch immediately or submit paperwork within ten days keeps a minor fender-bender from becoming a reporting violation.
sec11-card-sec11-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Four call police, ten days minor

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: What stopping, identification, and medical-aid duties apply immediately when a crash injures or kills someone?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Texas law requires staying on scene and arranging hospital or doctor care whenever an injured person needs or asks for help.
sec11-card-sec11-F04.must_match_memory_hook: Stop, stay, share info, render aid

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: After a crash that damages only attended vehicles, when and where must you move a drivable car before exchanging information?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Leaving two drivable cars parked in live freeway lanes over a dented bumper triggers far deadlier secondary highway pileups.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: What is the key action difference between stopping for an injury crash and stopping for a drivable vehicle-only crash?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Both require stopping and exchanging identification, yet unhurt drivers clear main traffic lanes first while injury scenes prioritize immediate aid.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: What prison terms and maximum fines punish fleeing a crash involving death, serious bodily injury, or other injury?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Panicking and driving away turns an accidental collision into a standalone felony carrying up to two decades behind prison bars.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: How do criminal charge levels step down across death, serious bodily injury, and other injury in a hit-and-run?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Even minor-injury hit-and-runs carry up to five years of state prison exposure, so fleeing never reduces legal trouble.
sec11-card-sec11-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Second-degree death, third-degree serious, prison injury

visual_sync.text_span: Second-degree death, third-degree serious, prison injury

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: What dollar threshold splits vehicle-damage hit-and-run penalties, and what fines or jail apply on each side of it?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Modern plastic bumpers easily pass two hundred dollars on a tiny parking-lot scrape, instantly putting six months of jail in play.
sec11-card-sec11-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Two hundred dollars triggers Class B

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: At what exact damage amount does fleeing a property-only crash jump from a Class C fine to Class B jail time?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Permit exams test that low two-hundred-dollar cutoff to remind drivers that almost any paint scratch crosses into jail territory.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: If you bump a parked unattended car, what must you do if you cannot find the owner, what goes in the note, and what penalties apply for leaving?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Tucking a blank phone number where wind blows it away fails Texas law — secure your name, address, and explanation visibly.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: What duties, reporting deadline, and fleeing penalties apply if your vehicle strikes highway landscaping, a signpost, or another roadside fixture?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Unlike bumping a parked car, hitting a guardrail or mailbox cannot be settled by taping a paper note onto bent metal.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: How do your legal options differ after hitting an unattended parked car versus hitting a roadside fixture or landscaping?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: City sign crews or property owners rarely walk past a damaged post the next hour, so direct owner notice replaces windshield notes.
sec11-card-sec11-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Cars allow notes, fixtures need notice

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: Why must hit-and-run victims file a police report for insurance, and what five rules guide bystanders helping an injured crash victim?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Adrenaline masks broken necks and internal trauma right after impact, and dragging someone carelessly can turn a spinal fracture into paralysis.
sec11-card-sec11-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Report hit-and-runs, never move injured victims

visual_sync.text_span: Report hit-and-runs, never move injured victims

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: What protects a hit-and-run victim's uninsured-motorist claim, and which five essentials protect an injured person at a crash scene?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Uninsured-motorist policies require an investigative trail, while steady pressure, warmth, and stillness keep crash victims stable until paramedics arrive.
sec11-card-sec11-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Report for coverage, pad, keep still

visual_sync.text_span: Report for coverage, pad, keep still

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: How does Texas traffic law classify a bicycle, and what rights and duties apply to its rider?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Test questions often bait you into treating cyclists like pedestrians, forgetting they follow vehicle rules whenever physically applicable.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: If you break a traffic law on a bicycle, how does the penalty compare to a car, and where does a conviction land?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Teens often think a bike ticket disappears, not realizing every conviction lands right on your permanent driving record.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: How must a cyclist treat traffic laws, stop signs, and red lights?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Rolling through an intersection on two wheels puts an unprotected rider straight into cross-traffic moving at full speed.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: In which direction must a bicyclist ride compared to surrounding traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Drivers pulling out of driveways scan left for cars, so riding against lanes puts you where nobody looks.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: What two foundational rules govern a bicyclist's travel direction and signal obedience?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Keep walkers and cyclists separate in your head because only foot traffic without a sidewalk faces oncoming cars.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: Where may a cyclist ride on a one-way street that has two or more marked lanes?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Watch out on your permit quiz because multi-lane one-way streets allow hugging the left curb instead of only the right.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: Where does a slower cyclist normally ride, and which four situations allow moving away from the right curb?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Taking a narrow lane under fourteen feet stops impatient drivers from squeezing past inches from your handlebars.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: How does a cyclist's curb edge position on a multi-lane one-way street compare to slower riding elsewhere?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: Test writers love swapping left and right edges between standard streets and multi-lane one-way roads to catch rushed readers.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: Under what two conditions may two cyclists ride abreast on a laned roadway?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Spilling across a lane line or holding up faster cars turns legal side-by-side riding into a roadway violation.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: Does Texas law allow a bicyclist to ride on the paved shoulder of a roadway?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Unlike motor vehicles that face strict passing limits on shoulders, cyclists can legally use that extra buffer space anytime.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: What four safety benefits do shared lane pavement markings provide for cyclists and drivers?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Following painted bike chevrons keeps cyclists clear of swinging car doors while alerting drivers to expect shared-lane traffic ahead.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: How do road shoulders, riding in pairs, and shared lane arrows each work for cyclists?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Combining legal shoulder space, single-lane pairing, and painted guides keeps traffic flowing smoothly without pinching riders against parked doors.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: Which specific arm positions do cyclists use to signal a right turn, a left turn, and a stop?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Drivers behind a bike have no brake lights or blinkers to read, so clear arm signals prevent sudden rear-end crashes.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: How do the two right-turn arm options differ from the left-turn and stop arm signals?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Permit tests check whether you know cyclists get a second right-turn option by extending their right arm straight out.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: How must a cyclist sit while riding, and how many riders may a bicycle carry?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Perched passengers on handlebars or rear pegs wreck steering balance and lengthen stopping distance in an emergency.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: May a bicyclist grab or attach onto a moving vehicle or streetcar on the roadway?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Grabbing a bumper or truck bed yanks a bike past safe balance speed where one pothole causes a severe fall.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: What limit applies to carrying packages, bundles, or objects while riding a bicycle?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Riding no-handed with bulky bags leaves you unable to brake or steer straight when hitting gravel or sudden bumps.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: Which three rider conduct rules govern bicycle seating, moving vehicles, and carrying items?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Every one of these three rules protects basic steering and braking control when sharing lanes with heavier traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: What exact stopping standard must every bicycle's brake meet in Texas?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Worn brake pads that only slow a wheel gradually cannot stop you in time when a car turns across.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: What equipment may a bicyclist with hearing loss display on their bike?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: A visible flag gives approaching drivers a heads-up that a horn tap alone might go unheard ahead.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: What front and rear night equipment must a bicycle carry, and from what distances must each required or optional item show?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Notice that an optional five-hundred-foot red tail lamp works alongside the approved rear reflector rather than replacing it.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: When riding after dark, which two items are mandatory on a bike and which rear item is optional?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: Quiz distractors often swap the mandatory rear reflector with the optional red tail light to test careful reading.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: At what level of government can bicycle helmet rules be made mandatory?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: Even without a blanket statewide adult mandate, city ordinances across Texas enforce local helmet rules you must obey.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: How should cyclists handle shared walkways, parked car rows, and stopping or fixing a bike?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: Weaving in and out between parked cars makes a rider vanish and reappear inside oncoming drivers' blind zones.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: How should a cyclist choose routes, and what gear or clothing helps drivers spot them?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Matching quieter streets to your comfort level while wearing bright reflective layers cuts crash risk before traffic gets heavy.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: Which three specific hazards must a bicyclist watch out for when riding in the rain?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: Wet metal covers and road paint lose tire grip instantly while rain-streaked windshields hide narrow bike silhouettes from drivers.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: How do local helmet ordinances, route choices, visibility gear, and rainy conditions tie together for cyclists?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Smart preparation before rolling out keeps small surprises like puddles, dim dusk light, or city ordinances from catching you.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: Whose directions override traffic signals and ordinary laws, where do you stop on steady red, and which two turns on red are lawful after yielding?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Watch the left-on-red trap: turning left after stopping on red works only when moving from one one-way street onto another one-way street.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: What action is required on flashing red, steady or flashing yellow, flashing yellow left arrows, steady green, and green arrows beside red?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Never assume cross traffic also faces a stop at flashing red, because intersecting lanes may still run steady green or flashing yellow.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: After making a complete stop, how do your travel options at a steady red light differ from a flashing red light?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Steady red keeps straight-through travel locked out until green, whereas flashing red acts like a stop sign once cross lanes clear.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: How do your duties differ across a steady yellow light, a flashing yellow light, and a flashing yellow left arrow?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Flooring the gas to beat a steady yellow invites T-bone wrecks, while misreading a flashing yellow arrow risks head-on left turns.
sec05-card-sec05-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Steady stops, flashing slows, arrow yields

visual_sync.text_span: Steady stops, flashing slows, arrow yields

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: How does driving on a steady green light compare with following a green arrow displayed beside a red light?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: A green arrow beside red opens only its pointed path, so drifting straight through the red lane draws an instant violation.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: What four core jobs do roadway traffic signs perform for drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Recognizing whether a sign warns, guides, informs, or regulates tells you immediately if a posted message is advisory or enforceable law.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: What meaning belongs to red, green, blue, yellow, black-and-white, orange, reflective orange, and brown road signs?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Rain, fog, or highway glare lets you read background color long before lettering sharpens, giving you extra seconds to react.
sec05-card-sec05-F04.must_match_memory_hook: Red stops, orange work, brown parks

visual_sync.text_span: Red stops, orange work, brown parks

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: What meaning belongs to each of the eight standard road-sign shapes, and what risk follows ignoring warning signs?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Written exams love testing the five-sided pentagon for schools, the sideways pennant for no-passing zones, and the round railroad notice.
sec05-card-sec05-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Octagon stop, pennant no-pass, circle rail

visual_sync.text_span: Octagon stop, pennant no-pass, circle rail

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: How do red, yellow, orange, and brown pair up with octagon, triangle, diamond, and pennant sign shapes?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Mud, glare, or faded paint can hide words, yet an eight-sided outline or downward triangle still commands instant action.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: How must you respond to warnings for low clearance, medians, added lanes, right-then-left reverse curves, joining roads, rough pavement, and signals ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Watch the added-lane versus merge exam trap: an added-lane diamond means incoming traffic gets its own lane without needing to merge.
sec05-card-sec05-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Added lane flows, reverse curve slows

visual_sync.text_span: Added lane flows, reverse curve slows

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: What actions follow warnings for sharp or gradual curves, winding roads, divided-highway endings, wet pavement, two-way traffic, crossroads, and lane drops?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Forgetting that a median just ended leads drivers to pull left into oncoming traffic as if still on a one-way freeway.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: How should you adjust speed, lane position, and passing for reverse curves, sharp turns, and gradual curves versus a winding road?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Shedding speed before entering the bend keeps tire grip planted while preventing blind head-on passing gambles.
sec05-card-sec05-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Slow down, keep right, never pass

visual_sync.text_span: Slow down, keep right, never pass

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: What hazards and driver responses pair with warnings for T and Y junctions, merges, pedestrian or school areas, loose gravel, pier obstructions, and alignment shifts?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Jamming the brakes or jerking the wheel on loose gravel breaks tire traction immediately and spins the rear end wide.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: How should you handle warnings for T must-turns, dips, soft shoulders, narrow or icy bridges, highway junctions, double sharp turns, and night delineators?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Cold wind chills elevated bridge decks from above and below, forming invisible black ice while ground-level asphalt still feels dry.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: Which four warning types belong to road junctions, and which four warn about changing road surfaces?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Grouping warnings into traffic-conflict junctions versus low-grip surfaces tells you whether to scan cross lanes or ease pedal inputs.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: What do warnings for traffic islands, bridge-rail ends, entering trucks, narrow or dirt transitions, edge drop-offs, wet-weather grooves, and wheelchair crossings tell you?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Yanking the wheel sharply back onto high pavement from a low shoulder drop-off slingshots cars straight into oncoming lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: How do you respond to warnings for steep downgrades, metered ramps, sudden humps, sharp curves, ending right lanes, stop signs ahead, and animal crossings?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Shifting into a lower gear lets engine compression hold speed down hills instead of overheating and fading your brake pads.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: What legal force do regulatory signs carry, and what rules do they set on arrow turns, weekday carpool hours, passing, double lefts, disabled spaces, and banned turns?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Notice the double-left nuance: the far-left lane must turn left, while the outer turn lane may also allow continuing straight.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: Why does slowing never satisfy a stop sign for any vehicle in line, and what other speed, passing, truck, and island rules appear on regulatory signs?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Piggybacking behind the car ahead without making your own complete stop at the line is a classic ticket and road-test fail.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: How does the legal demand of a stop sign compare with a posted curve advisory speed?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Rolling a stop sign breaks state law every time, whereas curve plaques show the safe speed ceiling before tires lose grip.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: What regulatory rules cover wrong-way entry, merging, flashing school zones, red-light cameras, double white lines, protected lefts, shoulders, detours, and single-file merges?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Using paved highway shoulders to sneak past rush-hour backups violates emergency-only rules and blocks incoming tow or medic units.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: What rules govern highway crossovers, school-zone phone bans, all-way stop ties, passing-only left lanes, shared center turn lanes, and dedicated turn lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Cruising down a shared center left-turn lane or camping slow in a passing-only left lane draws immediate citations in Texas.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: How do all-way stop tie-breakers, protected green arrows, center left-turn lanes, and passing-only far-left lanes work together?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Even under a protected green arrow, scanning before turning catches red-light runners and late crosswalk walkers.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: What duties and details come from route guide signs, railroad advance warnings, track-count crossbucks, and crossing emergency notification signs?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: A number plaque under the crossbuck warns when multiple tracks sit side by side, where one passing train can hide another.
sec05-card-sec05-F16.must_match_memory_hook: Never race trains, check track count

visual_sync.text_span: Never race trains, check track count

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: What do litter barrel notices, route shields, interstate mileposts, spurs or business routes, and overhead red-cross, yellow-cross, and green-arrow lane signals tell you?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Reversible commuter lanes flip direction by time of day, so driving underneath an overhead red cross puts you head-on with traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: How do advance railroad signs and crossbucks differ in placement, and how do overhead red crosses and green arrows control lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: Mixing up an early circular rail warning with the tracks-edge crossbuck causes late braking when heavy freight appears.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: When do lowering rail gates and warnings demand stops, and what rules govern two-lane broken lines, one-way lanes, double yellows, and center turn lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Accelerating to beat a gate arm that just started flashing red risks getting trapped right between the rails.
sec05-card-sec05-F18.must_match_memory_hook: Stop first flash, center turns only

visual_sync.text_span: Stop first flash, center turns only

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: How do broken lines and solid yellow lines control passing, and what distance window governs railroad crossing stops?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Check whichever yellow stripe hugs your own side of the centerline before pulling out to pass on a two-lane road.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: What do driver-side solid yellow, broken lines, crosswalks, white stop lines, left-edge freeway yellow, single solid white, and double solid white lines mean?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Yellow marks the left edge toward opposing traffic or medians, so crossing an interstate's left yellow stripe puts you off-road.
sec05-card-sec05-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Solid yellow left, double white bans

visual_sync.text_span: Solid yellow left, double white bans

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: What job do painted crosswalks and stop lines share, and how does a single solid white line differ from a double solid white line?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Exam questions test that exact jump in strictness: single solid white urges staying put, while double solid white makes lane changes illegal.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: What do crash barrels, hearing-impaired flags on bikes or cars, and orange diamond or rectangular work-zone devices mean, and when do construction fines double?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Watch the fine-doubling condition on exam day: construction-zone violation tickets double specifically when road crews are present.
sec05-card-sec05-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Orange work zone, workers double fines

visual_sync.text_span: Orange work zone, workers double fines

sec05-card-sec05-R12.question_text: What basic color identifies Texas work-zone traffic devices, and under what condition do construction-zone fines double?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: Empty cones overnight carry standard ticket amounts, whereas active road crews on-site immediately double the penalty.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: How must you drive past lit channelizers, sloping barricade stripes, arrow panels, orange-clad flaggers, and remote auto-flagger or pilot-car setups?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Barricade diagonal stripes slope downward toward the open lane, and swerving out of line when a flagger stops you endangers ground crews.
sec05-card-sec05-F21.must_match_memory_hook: Pass downward stripes, hold for flagger

visual_sync.text_span: Pass downward stripes, hold for flagger

sec05-card-sec05-R13.question_text: How do diagonal barricade stripes show which side to pass on, and how must you stop and wait for a work-zone flagger?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.teaching_text: Follow the direction a raindrop would slide down the diagonal stripe, and stay still in your lane until waved ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: How do penalties escalate for ignoring warning signs or driving past flooded-road barricades, and which machines may display a slow-moving vehicle emblem?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Mounting an orange triangle onto a mailbox or driveway post is illegal because drivers rely on it to spot slow rigs at night.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: Which six maneuvers require a signal, how may you give it day or night, how early do you start, and why cancel right after?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Leaving a blinker flashing after your move tricks cross-traffic into pulling directly across your bumper.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: Which everyday moves require signaling, how far ahead must your signal run before turning or stopping, and what comes right after turning?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Flicking your lever mid-turn warns nobody behind you and commonly costs easy points on road exams.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: Where is driving on the left half of the road banned, and what three exceptions let you leave the right side?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Crossing left near hills, curves, bridges, or crossings puts you nose-to-nose with hidden oncoming cars.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: Within one hundred feet of which structures and crossings is the left side off-limits, and when may you legally leave the right?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Test writers love pairing junctions, tracks, tunnels, and bridges with that exact hundred-foot no-left buffer.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: What four habits keep a pass safe, and what crash risk makes impatient passing so dangerous?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Forcing a tight gap or chopping back too sharply triggers high-speed head-on or sideswipe wrecks.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: How do you warn a driver before overtaking when needed, and how should you merge back into the lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Startling a drifting driver or clipping back across their front bumper turns routine passes fatal.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: What steps take you through a two-lane pass from initial checks to canceling your right signal, including oncoming and mirror cues?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Skipping blind-spot checks or cutting right before seeing headlights in your mirror invites instant contact.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: What oncoming clearance must you keep when passing, and what visual cue tells you it is safe to pull back right?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Two opposing cars close distance twice as fast, making misjudged gaps an exam-favorite trap.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: Under what road or shoulder conditions may you legally pass on the right in Texas, and what surface rule never bends?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Dropping tires onto dirt or gravel at highway speed spins cars straight back into traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: Which four vehicle situations let you pass on a paved shoulder, and what road setups allow normal right-side passing?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Texas permits paved-shoulder passes around stopped or left-turning traffic, yet driving off pavement remains illegal.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: How must you respond when another driver overtakes you, and what two choices keep an overtaker out of blind spots?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Racing a passer traps them in oncoming lanes, while hovering beside rear quarters hides your car.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: What speed and lane rules bind a driver being overtaken, including on unmarked roads, and how must passers treat blind spots?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Accelerating while someone passes stretches their exposure time and breaks Texas right-of-way safety law.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: How early must you reach your turn lane, what checks come first, and what should you do if you are within half a block?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Diving across lanes at the last second causes T-bone and sideswipe crashes at busy corners.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: How do you manage hand signals, braking, clutching, steering hands, and lane tracking right before and during a turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Braking hard mid-corner upsets tire grip, and steering one-handed during a hand signal slows recovery.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: What is the half-block lane rule, the turn-signal distance rule, and the hand-signal timing rule at an intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Combining early lane positioning with two-handed cornering prevents sudden cutoffs and wide, sloppy exits.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: From lane entry to exit, what are the exact steps and path for making a clean right turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Swinging left before turning right lures cyclists and trailing cars into squeezing past your inside.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: How do you stage, yield, and track relative to the center point when turning left on two-way streets, and which lane do you enter?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Cutting the corner early slices directly through the oncoming left-turn box on cross streets.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: How does your corner path and yielding duty on a right turn contrast with a two-way left turn?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Mixing up tight right-curb tracking with wider left-turn arcs leads to wrong-way lane entries.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: When turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street, which lane do you leave and which lane do you enter?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Forgetting that the cross street carries two-way traffic can put you head-on into its opposing side.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: Which lane should you enter when turning left onto a one-way street, and what overrides standard single-lane turn paths?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Multi-lane turn arrows and overhead signs often assign dedicated arcs that override default corner rules.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: Which signals govern pedestrians at intersections, and where should you wait before crossing?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Standing out in the roadway shaves away driver reaction space right where turning cars cut closest to corners.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: Where is crossing banned between intersections, which side of a crosswalk do you use, and when do you look both ways?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Stepping out mid-block or from behind parked cars hides you from oncoming drivers until braking distance disappears.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: How do signal waits, mid-block rules, and crosswalk positioning fit together for pedestrians?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Permit questions mix these three basics to spot test-takers who forget curb waiting or drift left inside busy crosswalks.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: Where must you walk first if available, and what do you do on a road without sidewalks?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Facing oncoming lanes lets you spot a drifting car early and step clear instead of getting struck from behind.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: What three-step order decides where a pedestrian walks and reacts to approaching vehicles?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Test distractors flip pedestrians onto the right edge with their backs turned, leaving zero warning when vehicles approach.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: Who gets the right-of-way when a pedestrian crosses outside an intersection crosswalk or skips a tunnel or overpass?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Drivers between intersections or under pedestrian bridges never expect foot traffic, so the law shifts yielding onto the walker.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: Which two pedestrian shortcuts both require yielding the right-of-way to every vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Many learners assume pedestrians always hold priority, missing the classic quiz trap whenever marked crossings or bridges get bypassed.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: Who may carry a white cane on public streets, and when is standing in a roadway to solicit allowed?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Protecting the white cane signal keeps drivers alert to vision loss while banning roadside hitchhiking prevents sudden lane swerves.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: Who holds exclusive public-road rights to a white cane, and what sole permission allows roadside fundraising?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Watch for trick choices claiming any charity can collect in traffic without getting approval from the local road authority.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: What six safety habits protect pedestrians around traffic, transit stops, car doors, night walks, alcohol, and local crossing bans?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Dark clothing, impaired judgment, and stepping out on the traffic side turn ordinary evening walks into preventable roadway collisions.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: Which three pedestrian rules target sudden street entries, nighttime visibility, and alcohol risk?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Headlights catch dark outfits late at night, and impaired judgment makes sudden step-outs impossible for drivers to dodge.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: What three actions should a driver take upon spotting someone crossing or about to cross the street?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Easing off the gas early and covering the brake buys crucial space if a pedestrian misjudges your speed.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: How must drivers respond when a pedestrian with a white cane or assistance animal is crossing or trying to cross?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: A pedestrian relying on sound or a guide animal cannot dodge a rolling bumper, making a complete stop essential.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: How does your duty toward general crossing pedestrians step up when a white cane is present?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Permit questions contrast ordinary caution with the stricter mandate to come to a dead stop whenever danger threatens blind pedestrians.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: At which four locations should drivers stay extra alert for blind pedestrians?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Heavy transit activity and crowded commercial blocks mask engine noise, making visual scanning vital for drivers in all four spots.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: When behind the wheel, what level of attention do you owe people on foot?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Unprotected people on foot absorb the full force of any mistake, so constant driver awareness outranks impatience on every street.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: What four habits and legal duties define a defensive driver in Texas?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: Insisting on your technical right-of-way never beats avoiding a wreck when another driver slips up right ahead.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: Who must buckle up in belt-equipped vehicles, which children need car seats, and what three crash dangers do belts prevent?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: Permit questions love testing both cutoffs at once, pairing age eight with the four-feet-nine-inches height threshold.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: How do Texas fine ranges compare across unbelted drivers, riders fifteen and older, small children, riders under seventeen, and open-bed minors?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Watch how responsibility lands on the driver with higher fine ceilings whenever younger passengers ride unsecured or unbuckled.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: Below what age are passengers barred from open pickup or trailer beds, and which six defenses apply?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: A hard brake or swerve launches unrestrained pickup-bed riders onto pavement, leaving only narrow exceptions like beaches or emergencies.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: What three core takeaways sum up Texas seatbelt rules, child safety seats, and fine severity?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Checking every passenger belt before shifting out of park protects your friends and spares you the steepest fines.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: When is towing a boat or personal watercraft with someone under eighteen aboard legal versus an offense?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Notice towed watercraft allow only three narrow defenses, fewer than the open-pickup-bed rule, so read answer choices closely.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: What criminal classification applies to riding inside a towed trailer or semitrailer, and which exceptions excuse it?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Unlike age-limited boat or pickup rules, enclosed cargo trailers ban occupants of any age unless a listed defense fits.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: What pattern links the passenger bans and common exceptions across open truck beds, towed boats, and towed trailers?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Keeping passengers inside belted cab seats eliminates rollover and ejection hazards while keeping you clear of misdemeanor charges.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: Which six vehicle steps should you complete as soon as an officer signals you to pull over?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: Shutting down the motor and flipping on the interior light after dark reassures the approaching officer immediately.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: Once parked for a traffic stop, how should you handle your hands, window, passengers, weapons, documents, and departure?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: Digging into a console or glovebox unannounced looks dangerous from outside, so always speak before moving your hands.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: Which three courtesy practices keep a roadside stop calm around seating, hand movement, and handgun storage?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: Storing a firearm in the same compartment as your insurance card forces risky hand movement near a weapon.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: What three core actions anchor safe parking, hand placement, and document retrieval during a police stop?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Predictable, unhurried body language turns a tense roadside encounter into a quick, routine check for everyone.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: What must you normally do for emergency lights behind you, and what three steps apply if the spot feels unsafe?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: Slowing way down with hazard flashers and calling dispatch proves you are complying rather than fleeing toward arrest.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: How does Texas balance immediate stops for police lights with personal safety on dark, isolated stretches?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Never speed up when looking for a well-lit lot because high speed turns a cautious roll into evasion.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: During a traffic stop or arrest, when does the right to silence apply, and what identification must you provide truthfully?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Staying quiet on investigative questions is legal, but withholding your driver license or giving fake details triggers arrest.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.question_text: Can you decline a vehicle search request, when may an officer search anyway, and how must you respond physically?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.teaching_text: Stating clearly that you do not consent preserves your legal rights in court, whereas physical interference brings charges.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: How do silence, driver licenses, and vehicle searches each work during a Texas traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Permit questions test where your constitutional protections end and mandatory driver cooperation begins on the roadside.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.question_text: What does signing a traffic ticket actually mean, and how should you handle any misconduct complaint?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.teaching_text: Refusing to sign on the shoulder risks arrest over a misunderstanding because your signature admits zero guilt.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: Why should you sign a citation calmly and save any dispute until after the traffic stop ends?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Courts and agency supervisors resolve disputes safely, while roadside arguments only escalate a routine ticket.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.question_text: What makes giving a fake name unlawful, and what two factors escalate the penalty for fleeing an officer?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.teaching_text: Driving or boating away from flashing lights upgrades evasion instantly, and injuring anyone makes penalties far harsher.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.question_text: What six calm driving habits help you defuse road rage and deal with aggressive drivers?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.teaching_text: Matching an angry tailgater's energy turns traffic delays into crashes, so clear space and report dangerous drivers.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: What are the legal and safety stakes for giving a false identity, evading detention, and road rage?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: Panic choices behind the wheel turn minor traffic moments into criminal charges or hundreds of preventable casualties.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.question_text: Which federal safety standard must a neighborhood electric vehicle meet, and what is its top flat-pavement speed?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.teaching_text: Memorize thirty-five miles per hour as the vehicle's built-in speed ceiling so you never confuse it with road limits.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.question_text: What five mechanical features define a legal motor-assisted scooter in Texas?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.teaching_text: Engines above forty cubic centimeters or frames lacking human-propulsion capability push a ride outside scooter rules.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.question_text: Up to what posted speed limits may neighborhood electric vehicles and motor-assisted scooters operate, and who can ban them?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.teaching_text: Notice a thirty-five-mile-per-hour neighborhood electric can use forty-five zones, while scooters cap out on thirty-five streets.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: How is a self-balancing assistive device built, and when and where may it use sidewalks, paths, or residential streets?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Self-balancing riders belong mainly on sidewalks and bike paths, entering quiet residential pavement only briefly at the right edge.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: What separates neighborhood electric vehicles, motor-assisted scooters, and self-balancing devices under Texas law?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: Permit exams mix posted street caps across all three rides, so keep forty-five, thirty-five, and sidewalk-first straight.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: Which six everyday habits make up the handbook's keys to safe driving?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: Putting courtesy ahead of stubborn right-of-way claims and skipping the wheel when unfit prevents wrecks before they start.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: How must truck cargo beds and tie-downs secure loads, and when do loose dirt-type loads require a tarp?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: Flying gravel and unlatched freight smash windshields behind you unless enclosed, dropped below bed walls, or tarped tight.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.question_text: Which vehicles must connect DPS-approved safety chains when pulling a trailer, and which two setups are exempt?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.teaching_text: If a trailer coupler pops loose at highway speed, approved safety chains keep the tongue from veering into oncoming lanes.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: What length, strength, flag size, vehicle count, and cargo exception apply to tow links and bars?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: Drivers turning across gaps can easily miss a low tow cable without that bright twelve-inch white cloth warning.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.question_text: How do Texas hauling laws lock down loose cargo, light-duty trailers, and tow connections?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.teaching_text: Unsecured cargo, unchained hitches, and invisible tow lines turn heavy highway gear into sudden roadway obstacles.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: Which five habits prevent carbon monoxide poisoning around vehicles, and what two steps help a victim?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: Odorless exhaust gas builds up fast inside garages or leaky cabins, knocking occupants unconscious before they notice symptoms.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.question_text: Why is vehicle exhaust called a silent threat, what does it forbid, and what is first aid for exposure?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.teaching_text: Even an open garage door can trap deadly fumes around a warming car, so always pull outside immediately.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: Which two optional forms let Texans with communication challenges add a driver license code and a vehicle registration alert?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: Alerting dispatch ahead of time helps an approaching officer understand delayed speech, deafness, or autism without misreading behavior.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.question_text: How do Texas's optional communication indicators protect drivers and passengers during a roadside stop?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.teaching_text: Giving officers advance context before they reach your window prevents misunderstandings when spoken instructions are hard to process.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: Who needs a Texas driver license, and how do the rules treat ninety-day newcomers, non-farm machines, sixteen-plus or eighteen-plus nonresidents, and military members?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Practice questions love tangling nonresident age thresholds with the grace windows granted to newcomers and active-duty troops.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: How does the Texas ninety-day license clock for new residents differ from the rule for active-duty military drivers?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Both rules share the exact same day count, so check whether someone just moved to Texas or is leaving active service.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: Who must ride beside a Texas learner driver, who can apply, what do teen versus restricted adult cards cost, and what happens to old cards?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Your front-seat co-pilot must stay alert and unimpaired with a year of licensed experience, and prior cards get surrendered first.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: How do the total price and expiration window compare between a teen learner card and a practicing adult's restricted license?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Distractors regularly swap the sixteen-dollar teen card ending at eighteen with the adult eight-year price tag.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: If you are under eighteen applying for the first time, what attendance or diploma benchmarks must your school VOE show, and how fresh must it be?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Walking into the licensing counter with an expired school verification form turns your appointment into an automatic turn-away.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: How long does a signed school VOE stay valid during the school year versus during summer break?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Campus offices shut down over break, so summer forms stay good three times longer than school-year ones.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: How can a fifteen- to eighteen-year-old qualify for a hardship license, and what exam and hold rules govern Texas graduated licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Wanting an early ride for convenience never qualifies; an authorized adult must petition in person over four narrow emergencies.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: What separates qualifying for a hardship license from completing graduated Phase One?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Any license suspension during your learner phase tacks extra days onto that mandatory waiting clock before advancing.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: Once you reach Phase Two of graduated licensing, what three limits restrict passengers, overnight driving, and wireless devices?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Loading extra friends into the car or tapping a phone under eighteen outside an emergency violates your provisional terms.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: In graduated Phase Two, how do the young-passenger cap and the midnight-to-five curfew apply independently?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Driving completely alone at two in the morning still breaks curfew unless the trip is for work, school, or an emergency.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: Who gets PROVISIONAL or UNDER twenty-one cards, how do out-of-state teens place in GDL, how long do adult cards run, and what about commercial-exempt rigs?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Being exempt from commercial rules never lets you steer heavy Class A or B rigs on a basic car license.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: How does the age range for a PROVISIONAL marking differ from an UNDER twenty-one marking on a Texas license?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Older teens age out of the provisional label at eighteen while keeping the under-twenty-one banner for three more years.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: What vehicles and trailer weights do non-commercial Class A and Class B licenses cover, do they cover motorcycles, and what do they cost?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Even the top heavy-truck class excludes two-wheel motorcycles unless you add the dedicated motorcycle endorsement.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: How does the weight test for needing a Class A license differ from the weight test for Class B?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Check the towed load in every weight question, because heavy trailer weight pushes combinations into the highest class.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: What vehicles and three fee tiers belong to Class C, and what course or teen credentials are required for Class M?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Certified three-wheel autocycles run legally on a car license, whereas two-wheel motorcycles demand state-approved rider training.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: How does the fee to append Class M onto an active license compare with the extra fee when renewing Class M?

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: Who can get a Texas ID card, how is it oriented and priced by age, and how do emergency contacts or allergy drugs go on the back?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Since DPS never prints medical records onto cards, handwriting allergy medications next to two emergency contacts aids responders.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: What does the heart donor mark establish, which five causes can applicants fund, and how do voter offers and Selective Service work at DPS?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Applicants within two months of eighteen get an in-person voter prompt, while young men eighteen to twenty-five register automatically.
